title: OPERATION LOW WATER
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} border, {YEAR}. {EMPLOYER} wants the Project HALBERD test articles out of {TARGET_FACTION}'s proving annex before the trial cycle finishes and the hardware is crated for shipment to the rear. {NPC:intel-source} places the package — 2 sensor-mast assemblies and 1 fire-control core, 1.9 tons crated — in Test Shed 4 on days 5 and 6 of each 6-day trial cycle. That report is 9 days old, so treat the schedule as likely but not certain. The current cycle began on day-of-month 11; your window is the night of day 15 into day 16. Miss it and the package is on the range, dispersed across 4 instrumented firing lanes, and your clean lift becomes a search under fire. The annex sits on the west bank of a lowland river, 31 kilometers west of the district capital, where the garrison keeps 1 BattleMech company and its armor. The only vehicle bridge crosses at the capital itself, checkpointed, 4 minutes from the garrison gate. Everything else is the river shallows: 3 cobble-bottom fords — North, Middle, South — spread along 7 kilometers of floodplain. At survey datum the fords run 0.8 to 1.4 meters deep. BattleMechs cross all 3 at any surveyed depth. Wheeled support cannot cross anything deeper than 1.1 meters, and the spring rain coming off the highlands adds an estimated 0.3 meters for every 12 hours of sustained rain. The shallows are your only way in and out, so rising water can strand you on the wrong bank. Annex security is 2 motorized infantry platoons, 2 light SecurityMechs (20-ton class, fitted with searchlights), and a range-safety radar on the water tower that also serves as an air-watch set: any powered descent within 40 kilometers is logged and flagged to the garrison within 3 minutes. This radar report is 16 days old and probably still current, but plan as if the tower may have been upgraded since. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands at the district capital and has rehearsed a river-line response twice this quarter: the quick-reaction lance moves to the bridge first, holds it, and lets the river itself act as the cordon. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. The fire-control core can withstand only 2 g of shock while crated; it must ride on a padded carrier or it will be destroyed in transit. The fire-control core is the contract — that is what you are paid to deliver. The two sensor masts are a bonus. And the river crossing sets your whole timetable: the weather decides how long your window stays open.

objectives.primary: Seize the Project HALBERD fire-control core from Test Shed 4 intact (shock-limit 2 g) and deliver it to the extraction DropShip.
objectives.secondary: Seize both sensor-mast assemblies (0.6 tons each) or, failing seizure, destroy them in the shed.
objectives.bonus: Copy or remove the trial-cycle data ledgers from the annex range office, 200 meters north of Shed 4.

complications.name: Rising Water
complications.text: A rain cell is forecast across the highlands inside your operational window. Each 12 hours of sustained rain adds an estimated 0.3 meters at all 3 fords. At +0.3 the wheeled carrier option dies; at +0.6 even 'Mech crossings take the current penalty.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track a rain clock from mission start. At +12h of rain: wheeled vehicles cannot ford. At +24h: 'Mechs fording treat water hexes as depth +1 and make a piloting check mid-river while carrying the core.

complications.name: Cycle Slip
complications.text: The trial cycle is reconstructed from a 9-day-old source. If {TARGET_FACTION} slipped one day, the package is on the firing lanes, not in Shed 4 — dispersed across 4 instrumented positions over 2 kilometers of range.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a 1-in-3 at mission generation, the objective relocates to the range lanes: add 12 minutes of on-site search and 1 additional contact with a SecurityMech patrol.

complications.name: Air-Watch Tower
complications.text: The range-safety radar logs powered descents inside 40 kilometers and flags them to the district capital within 3 minutes. A flagged descent starts the garrison reaction clock at touchdown, not at first contact.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If ingress Option C is chosen, or any powered approach is unmasked, the reaction timeline starts at landing. Destroying the tower (1 structure point, exposed) silences it but is itself an alarm.

complications.name: Fragile Cargo
complications.text: The crated fire-control core can take only 2 g of shock. A 'Mech carrying the crate in its hands and moving faster than a walk will exceed that limit on rough ground and damage the core. The padded wheeled carrier prevents this, but the carrier is also the piece of equipment most likely to be stranded or swamped at a rising ford, so protecting the core and getting the carrier across pull against each other.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Core aboard a running 'Mech or a jolted vehicle: roll 2d6 each turn of rough movement; on 4 or less the core degrades to PARTIAL objective value.

decisionPoints.name: Ingress — Crossing the River Problem
decisionPoints.context: The annex is on the west bank of the river. The garrison and the only bridge are on the east bank. Your choice of approach decides which threat sets your timing: the air-watch radar, the rising river, or the garrison reaction force.

options.title: Option A — West Floodplain Night Drop
advantages: No river crossing inbound — you start on the objective bank
Drop profile timed against the radar's 11-second sweep gap keeps the descent unflagged on a competent insertion
disadvantages: Drop scatter onto a soaked floodplain — each 'Mech rolls landing displacement up to 800 meters
The DropShip cannot ground west-bank; exfiltration still crosses the river shallows with the core aboard
options.consequence: You start dry but finish wet. Because there is no inbound crossing, the whole garrison reaction window is spent on the way out, at the fords, carrying the core. If the rain holds, the fords are 0.3 meters higher at mission end than they were at the start, so the crossing you planned for is harder than the one you scouted.

costs.resource: 4 drop cocoons expended; the padded carrier cannot drop with you — the core rides 'Mech hands at walking speed the whole way out
costs.risk: Scatter up to 800 m per 'Mech on landing; one piloting check mid-river with the core aboard if the rain holds the fords at +0.3 m

options.title: Option B — Quarry Ground Approach
advantages: DropShip grounds masked in an abandoned aggregate quarry 22 km south — no powered descent inside the radar's flag radius
Approach on firm haul roads; the padded wheeled carrier comes with you, solving the shock problem outright
disadvantages: 3.1 hours of road movement each way past 2 farm hamlets — civilian observation reaching the district capital in 4–8 hours is the planning assumption
The carrier must ford South Shallows twice; any rain accumulation past +0.3 m strands it
options.consequence: This is the slowest approach but the safest for the cargo, because the padded carrier comes with you and removes the shock risk. The cost is two new problems: civilians at the hamlets may report you, and that report can reach the garrison while the raid is still underway; and the carrier can only cross while the fords stay low, so any significant rain strands it on the wrong bank.

costs.resource: padded wheeled carrier committed forward — stranded outright if the fords rise past +0.3 m
costs.risk: Civilian observation at 2 hamlets starts a 4-8 hour report clock that can mature mid-raid

options.title: Option C — East Bank Hard Landing
advantages: Ground 6 km from the bridge, demonstrate against it, and force {NPC:opfor-commander} to hold his QRF at the crossing he believes you need
Shortest total timeline — 40 minutes of planned ground time
disadvantages: The radar flags you at descent; the reaction clock starts before your feet are dry
You must still put a snatch element across Middle Shallows and back while the demonstration holds attention
options.consequence: The garrison reacts to the bridge, which is the wrong place, for as long as the demonstration holds its attention. The risk is timing: if the garrison sees through the demonstration before your snatch team has crossed back, the quick-reaction lance turns to the fords and arrives while your team is still in the river.

costs.resource: demonstration ammunition: one lance combat load expended against the bridge before the objective is touched
costs.risk: Radar flags the descent — the garrison reaction clock starts at touchdown, not at first contact

entries.event: Annex alarm — perimeter contact or flagged descent reported to the district garrison TOC.
Garrison TOC confirms; QRF lance (4 'Mechs, Regular) ordered to the vehicle bridge.
QRF lance holds the bridge; 2 Scorpion light tanks begin east-bank river patrol toward North Shallows.
QRF lance releases from the bridge toward the annex if it is confirmed quiet; armor reaches North Shallows overlook.
Full company response achievable at the annex — 'Mech company plus 8 armor vehicles.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+25:00 — anything still west of the river shallows when the company closes is cut off against a rising river. Be across and moving by T+22:00.

opforSketch.composition: Annex site: 2 motorized infantry platoons, 2 light SecurityMechs (20-ton band), static searchlights. Garrison band: 1 mixed 'Mech company, Regular quality, light/medium bias with 1 heavy anchor; 8–12 armor vehicles (Vedette/Scorpion mix), the combined-arms weight the QRF leans on. No aerospace on-world; VTOL recon section only.
opforSketch.behavior: Doctrine is river-line containment: hold the bridge, patrol the fords, let the water cordon the raider. {NPC:opfor-commander} commits the QRF to the annex itself only after the bridge is confirmed secure. Expect deliberate, rehearsed, unimaginative — and therefore predictable to the minute.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG AUDIT
forks.trigger: The trial ledgers (bonus objective) name the second HALBERD test site and its shipment schedule.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} offers an immediate follow-on raid against the second site while {TARGET_FACTION} still believes the loss was isolated.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN SCALE
forks.trigger: The core is lost, destroyed past 2 g, or never seized; {TARGET_FACTION} parades the intact program on regional broadcast within 20 days.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} buys a denial strike: return to {WORLD} against a reinforced annex to destroy the program outright. Same ground, twice the garrison.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY CROSSING
forks.trigger: Any element is identified by unit insignia or recovered equipment during the raid.
forks.consequence: {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence opens a file on the unit; for the next 2 contracts in {TARGET_FACTION} space, treat garrison intelligence quality as one grade higher.

storyElementSeed: A tech kneels in river mud at the ford's edge, taping a moisture seal over a crate seam while 'Mech feet shift gravel upstream. Nobody speaks until the tape is down.

merc.objectives.primary: Seize the HALBERD fire-control core intact (shock-limit 2 g) and deliver per contract Annex C. Damage past 2 g voids the delivery bonus — the employer's assessor will check the crate telltales before releasing escrow.

rainGainPer12h.unit: meters added per 12 hours of rain

garrisonArmor.unit: armor vehicles at the district capital

phases.name: INGRESS — REACHING THE WRONG BANK
phases.lead: How you arrive decides which threat sets your timing. The water-tower radar flags any powered descent within 40 kilometers and reports it to the garrison within 3 minutes, and the garrison's quick-reaction force is only 4 minutes from its own gate. Decide before you cross whether you are bringing the padded carrier, because once you are on the west bank the rising river may make it impossible to send back for it.

dataBlock.Radar flag radius: 40 km — powered descents logged and flagged to the district garrison within 3:00 of detection
dataBlock.Sweep gap: 11 seconds per rotation; a timed unpowered descent can slip through it. This figure is 16 days old — probably right, but the whole night-drop plan rests on it
dataBlock.Garrison geometry: 1 'Mech company plus armor at the district capital, 31 km east; the only vehicle bridge is checkpointed, 4 minutes from the garrison gate
dataBlock.Descent abort threshold: any annex patrol observed outside the wire on the west floodplain during final approach

sidebarKernel.kernel: The 11-second radar sweep gap is a 16-day-old figure, and the entire night-drop plan depends on it being accurate. Make the uncertainty plain: the number is probably right but not guaranteed, and the whole insertion is being staked on it. Tell the crew what to watch for that would signal the radar has been upgraded since the report — a faster sweep, a second antenna, a descent flagged that should not have been.

phases.name: GROUND — SHED 4
phases.lead: Everything at the annex is built around the core. Breach Shed 4, check the crate's shock telltales to confirm the core is undamaged, and get the 1.9-ton package onto its padded carrier before a searchlight finds the breach. The range-office ledgers, 200 meters north, are the bonus objective. Going after them costs minutes, and those are minutes you may need later for the river crossing, so treat the ledgers as optional.

dataBlock.Shed 4 package: 1 fire-control core (shock-limit 2 g, crated) + 2 sensor-mast assemblies (0.6 tons each) — 1.9 tons total
dataBlock.Annex posting: 2 motorized infantry platoons on a 3-post rotation; 2 SecurityMechs (20-ton band) walking opposed perimeter laps, searchlights live from dusk
dataBlock.Range office: 200 m north of Shed 4; trial-cycle ledgers in a keyed cabinet — 4 minutes to force and pull
dataBlock.Cycle-slip check: package in Shed 4 on trial days 5–6 only, per a source 9 days old; an empty shed means a 12-minute search on the firing lanes and 1 additional patrol contact

phases.protocol: Use these short code phrases on the shared radio net. BONE DRY: the core is crated, padded, and moving. LOW WATER: the crossing team has started across a ford. HIGH WATER: the assigned ford is no longer usable, so switch to the named backup and report again. CUT BAIT: leave the sensor masts behind, the core comes first, and all teams head for the exit ford at the fastest safe speed. Keep every message to two words or fewer, because the garrison can track radio signals to their source — it does this slowly, but it does it, and long transmissions give it the time it needs.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — THE CALDER SHALLOWS
phases.lead: The raid ends at whichever ford is still passable once the rain has done its work. Be across the river and moving east by T+22:00. At T+25:00 the full garrison company closes the river line, and any force still on the west bank is trapped there — under siege, still holding the fragile core it was sent to recover.

dataBlock.North Shallows: 0.9 m at datum, 140 m wide, cobble bottom — overlooked from the east-bank bluff the armor patrol reaches at T+17:00
dataBlock.Middle Shallows: 1.2 m at datum, 90 m wide — 'Mech-passable at survey depth; already past the 1.1 m wheeled limit before any rain falls
dataBlock.South Shallows: 0.8 m at datum, 220 m wide — the only wheeled-capable crossing, and it dies past datum +0.3 m on the rain clock
dataBlock.Rain gauge: +0.3 m at all 3 fords per 12 hours of sustained rain; the forecast cell sits inside your operational window
dataBlock.Core crossing rule: core fords on padding at walking speed — one piloting check mid-river at +0.3 m or worse

sidebarKernel.kernel: Explain what the 2-g shock limit means in the middle of a ford: a single stumble in 1.2 meters of moving water can jolt the crate past 2 g and ruin the core the team is being paid to deliver. Cover the rules that prevent it — cross at walking speed only, tape the crate seams against moisture before the first ford, and carry the crate in the hand on the downstream side so the current pushes it against the 'Mech rather than away from it.

assetDetails.detail: The core is 0.7 tons of the 1.9-ton crated package. Its shock limit is 2 g, and the crate carries telltales that record any jolt above that — the employer's assessor reads them before releasing the delivery bonus, so a single rough excursion can cost the payment even if the core still works. Carry it on the padded carrier whenever the carrier is with you; carried in a 'Mech's hands it moves at walking speed only. Tape the crate seams against moisture before attempting the first ford.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Option A — West Floodplain Night Drop
resourceGates.lackingText: No owned DropShip: contracted lift will not fly the 11-second sweep-gap profile. Repriced as contracted night insertion at 40,000 C-bills plus a 12,000 hazard surcharge — and the descent is flagged, starting the reaction clock at landing.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Option C — East Bank Hard Landing
resourceGates.lackingText: No contracted carrier grounds inside a flagged radar radius to draw fire as a demonstration. Without an owned DropShip this option is unavailable.

title: OPERATION SILENT TIMETABLE
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} border, {YEAR}. {EMPLOYER}'s quartermaster analysts have spent 3 months working out how {TARGET_FACTION} keeps raiding the border when its supply lines look too thin to support the effort. The answer is on {WORLD}: a transshipment cache, Yard K-9, built into the elevated maglev line where it crosses the badlands, 26 kilometers east of the district capital. {NPC:intel-source}, a freight-forwarding clerk whose shipping ledgers {EMPLOYER} quietly purchased, records 4 bunkered magazines holding an estimated 380 tons of munitions and 12 tons of Class A 'Mech spare parts, stockpiled for the next raiding season. Those ledgers are 21 days old, so treat the tonnages as a solid estimate, not an exact count. If you destroy this cache, the enemy cannot supply that season's raids and will have to cancel or delay them. The terrain problem is the maglev line itself. The viaduct — 60 kilometers of elevated guideway on 14-meter pylons — is the only firm route across the badlands. Off the viaduct's service road, the gully fields slow 'Mechs to one-third speed and stop wheeled vehicles entirely. The viaduct is also the enemy's fastest way to reach you: from the district capital, the rail line can deliver an infantry company or the armored security train in 12 minutes at full line speed. That train, nicknamed the Yard Dog, mounts 2 autocannon in armored turrets and patrols the line every 40 minutes, give or take 10 — a schedule drawn from the same 21-day-old ledgers, so expect some drift. The yard garrison is 1 infantry company (Green, mostly conscripts), 6 wheeled APCs, 2 ZSU-pattern flak vehicles, and a yard officer who has standing authority to demolish the magazines — they are already wired for it, and {TARGET_FACTION} doctrine here is to blow the cache rather than let it be captured. {NPC:opfor-commander} at the district capital commands a 'Mech company and 1 aerospace flight; the flight needs 30 minutes from alert to takeoff. Sixty conscripted rail laborers sleep within 90 meters of Magazine 2; both {EMPLOYER}'s government and your next employer will read the civilian-casualty figures in your after-action report. Power for the line runs through Substation Pylon 212, 9 kilometers south of the yard — fenced, lit, and guarded by 1 squad. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}.

objectives.primary: Destroy all 4 bunkered magazines at Yard K-9 before the yard officer executes denial demolition on his own terms (a controlled {TARGET_FACTION} demolition preserves the rail plant and half the spares — yours must not).
objectives.secondary: Seize up to 12 tons of Class A 'Mech spares from the transit shed and load them on the captured flatbed consist or your own transport.
objectives.bonus: Capture the dispatch office manifest set — routing data identifying the destination world of the next raiding season's first strike.

complications.name: The Yard Dog
complications.text: The security trainset patrols the Spine on a 40-minute headway with 2 autocannon barbettes and a searchlight car. It arrives at line speed and fights from the elevated guideway — 14 meters up, hull-down behind the parapet.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll the Yard Dog's arrival on a 40±10 minute cycle from T+0. While the line is powered it functions as a mobile turret on the viaduct; if Substation Pylon 212 is destroyed, it coasts to a stop within 3 kilometers and fights as a static position.

complications.name: Pre-Wired Denial
complications.text: The magazines are wired for command demolition from the yard firing room. If the yard officer reaches it after the alarm, he blows Magazine 3 — the munitions stack — himself, denying you the catastrophic sympathetic detonation that makes the primary objective cheap.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From T+0 the yard officer is a moving timer: 8 minutes to the firing room unless the room (mapped, north end of the dispatch block) is seized or its trunk line cut first. If he fires, primary objective requires demolishing each remaining magazine individually — +20 minutes of engineering work under fire.

complications.name: Static Season
complications.text: The badlands generate dry electrical storms through this season. Inside a storm cell, communications beyond 2 kilometers fail and target-sharing degrades.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll each 30 minutes: on 1-in-3 a storm cell sits over the yard for the next 30 minutes — no indirect fire, no comms between yard element and any element beyond 2 km, all sensor ranges halved (both sides).

complications.name: Sixty Laborers
complications.text: The conscript rail crews barrack 90 meters from Magazine 2. They are not combatants and will scatter unpredictably at the first detonation — across firing lanes, onto the guideway, into the spares shed.
complications.mechanicalEffect: After the first detonation, each fire mission or demolition adjacent to the barracks block risks civilian casualties; accumulate any and the COMPROMISED fork triggers regardless of other outcomes.

decisionPoints.name: Ingress — Riding or Fighting the Spine
decisionPoints.context: The viaduct is three things at once: your only fast way in, the enemy's only fast way to reach you, and the structure the target cache is built into. Each approach below uses one of those facts to your advantage and accepts the others as risks.

options.title: Option A — Gully Field Approach
advantages: Drop 18 km south in the badlands and approach beneath sensor coverage — the gully walls mask 'Mech-height movement to within 2 km of the yard
No interaction with line dispatch, headway schedules, or the Yard Dog until you choose to begin
disadvantages: One-third movement for 16 of the 18 kilometers — 2.6 hours of approach, fatigue and heat accumulating before first contact
Wheeled salvage transport cannot follow; the secondary objective rides home on 'Mech hands or a captured consist only
options.consequence: You arrive undetected with the full garrison reaction window still ahead of you. The trade-off is that you have no vehicle support, so the only way to carry off the 'Mech spares is to capture rail rolling stock at the yard intact — if that fails, the spares stay behind.

costs.resource: 2.6 hours of approach through the gullies, spending heat and crew fatigue before the first shot; no wheeled transport, so the spares can only leave on captured rail cars
costs.risk: Nothing is risked until you make contact — the price of this option is paid entirely in time, plus the gamble that you can seize working rail cars for the spares

options.title: Option B — Captured Consist
advantages: Seize the freight maglev at a decommissioned quarry siding (1 caretaker, no garrison), ride the spine into the yard at line speed — 11 minutes of transit, arriving inside the wire
The consist itself becomes the spares-haul solution for the secondary objective
disadvantages: Single point of failure: if dispatch de-energizes the line en route, the consist coasts dead on the viaduct, 14 meters up, with your assault element aboard
'Mechs cannot ride; they follow on the service road and arrive 40 minutes behind the assault element
options.consequence: This is the fastest way in, but it creates a 40-minute window in which your infantry holds the yard alone before the 'Mechs arrive on foot. The danger is the rail line's power: if the enemy cuts it while you are still riding, the train stops dead on the viaduct, 14 meters above the ground, and your first task becomes rescuing your own stranded assault team instead of attacking the cache.

costs.resource: the captured train, which is the single point of failure for both your assault team and your means of hauling the spares out
costs.risk: If the enemy cuts line power while you are aboard, the assault team is stranded 14 meters up on a dead viaduct and the raid begins with a rescue

options.title: Option C — Shift-Change Combat Drop
advantages: Drop cocoons directly onto the yard at the 0400 shift change, when the garrison's posture is at its documented worst
All elements arrive together; the firing-room race starts with you 400 meters from the door instead of 2 kilometers
disadvantages: Immediate, total alarm — every clock in the reaction timeline starts at canopy-open
Drop scatter among pylons, catenary masts, and bunker roofs; each 'Mech risks landing damage in obstructed hexes
options.consequence: You give up all stealth in exchange for landing right on top of the objective. From that point the raid is a straight race between how fast you can set and blow the demolitions and the garrison's 30-minute clock to get aerospace fighters overhead.

costs.resource: drop cocoons, which are single-use; there is no plan to recover them from a defended yard
costs.risk: Drop scatter among the pylons, overhead power masts, and bunker roofs means each 'Mech rolls for landing damage in obstructed terrain

entries.event: Yard alarm — dispatch flashes the district garrison TOC; yard officer begins his 8-minute move to the firing room.
Line dispatch halts civilian traffic; Yard Dog ordered in from its patrol position (arrival per headway roll).
Earliest Yard Dog arrival at K-9 if the line is powered and the headway favors it.
Garrison 'Mech lance departs the district capital on the highway parallel to the spine — 26 km at flank patrol speed.
Aerospace flight wheels-up from the district capital field; on-station over the yard 8 minutes later.
Full company response achievable at K-9 with flak carriers integrated.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+38:00 — the aerospace flight on-station ends safe DropShip operations in the badlands. All elements aboard and lifting by T+38:00 or the ship leaves for the alternate pickup 200 km south and you walk the gullies.

opforSketch.composition: Yard: 1 Green infantry company, 6 wheeled APCs, 2 flak carriers, pre-wired demolitions, the Yard Dog trainset (2 AC barbettes, treat as medium-vehicle band). Garrison band: 1 {TARGET_FACTION} 'Mech company, Regular, medium-weight bias; 1 aerospace flight (2 fighters, Regular). Generator should weight the yard fight infantry-and-vehicle-heavy and the relief fight 'Mech-standard.
opforSketch.behavior: Yard force fights from prepared positions and stalls — their doctrine is to hold until denial demolition, not to win. The relief column moves fast on the highway and deploys conservatively at 2 km; {NPC:opfor-commander} has written orders not to lose 'Mechs defending stores, but the aerospace flight has no such caution.

forks.name: OPERATION COLD MANIFEST
forks.trigger: The dispatch manifests (bonus objective) name the first-strike world and its supply window.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} contracts the unit to be waiting on that world when the now-unsupplied raid arrives anyway — a defensive ambush with the enemy's own timetable in hand.

forks.name: OPERATION HOT SIDING
forks.trigger: The magazines survive substantially intact, or the {TARGET_FACTION} controlled demolition preserves the spares stock.
forks.consequence: The raiding season proceeds early: within 40 days the unit is offered emergency garrison reinforcement on the border world the cache was feeding, at standard rates against a prepared offensive.

forks.name: OPERATION RETURNED LETTER
forks.trigger: Civilian casualties among the rail laborers, or the freight clerk's ledger trail is exposed during the raid.
forks.consequence: {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence traces {NPC:intel-source} within 9 days. {EMPLOYER} offers a short-notice, unpaid-goodwill extraction of the clerk and family from the district capital — decline it and lose the intelligence network for the region.

storyElementSeed: In the dispatch office, a captured timetable board still updates itself, clicking through arrivals that will never come. A soldier watches it cycle twice before pulling the drive.

merc.situation: Frame it as a contract, not a campaign: the cache is the job, but the dispatch manifests are worth more, because they name the enemy's next target and the employer will pay extra for them. The contract pays a destruction bonus for each magazine you confirm destroyed — read Annex B before the mission, because it defines exactly what 'destroyed' has to look like to the employer's assessor, and a half-wrecked magazine may not count.

trainHeadwayMinutes.unit: minutes between Yard Dog patrol passes

cacheSparesTons.unit: tons of Class A spares in the transit shed

railLaborers.unit: conscript laborers barracked at the yard

phases.name: INGRESS — THE SPINE QUESTION
phases.lead: The maglev line is the fastest way in, the enemy's fastest way to reach you, and the structure the cache is built into. The ingress options decide which of those works for you and which works against you. Whatever you choose, plan to deal with Substation Pylon 212 before the first charge is set: it powers the rail line, and line power is the one thing both sides depend on — you to ride or block the line, the enemy to rush in reinforcements and run the Yard Dog.

dataBlock.Line speed delivery: district capital to K-9 in 12 minutes at line speed — for their reinforcements, or for your captured consist
dataBlock.Yard Dog headway: 40 minutes, plus or minus 10, between patrol passes — from ledgers 21 days old, so expect some drift
dataBlock.Substation Pylon 212: 9 km south; fenced, lit, 1 squad — destroyed, the Yard Dog coasts to a stop within 3 km and fights as a static position
dataBlock.Gully fields: 'Mech movement at one-third off the viaduct service road; wheeled transport does not survive off-road at all

sidebarKernel.kernel: Work out whether the demolition charges you are carrying leave enough to also destroy Substation Pylon 212. The substation is guarded by only 1 squad — about a tenth of the yard's garrison — and the payoff is large: with line power cut, the Yard Dog coasts to a stop within 3 km and fights as a fixed position on the ground, instead of moving up and down the viaduct shooting at you from behind its parapet 14 meters up.

phases.name: GROUND — THE YARD RACE
phases.lead: From the first alarm you are running two races at once. The first is your breach teams against the yard officer's 8-minute walk to the firing room, where he can detonate the magazines himself. The second is your demolition work against a garrison whose plan is simply to stall you until that happens. Magazine 3 is the munitions stack: blowing it sets off the other magazines in a chain reaction and does most of the primary objective's work for you — which is exactly why the yard officer will fire it first if he reaches the firing room.

dataBlock.Firing room: north end of the dispatch block, 1 armored door; the yard officer's clock runs 8:00 from T+0 unless the room is seized or its trunk line cut
dataBlock.Magazine 3: the munitions stack — if you detonate it, the blast chain-reacts through the other magazines and does most of the primary objective for you; if the yard officer fires it first, the {TARGET_FACTION} controlled demolition vents the blast and saves about half the spares
dataBlock.Laborer barracks: 90 meters from Magazine 2 — 60 conscripts who scatter across firing lanes at the first blast; sequence Magazine 2 last or clear the block first
dataBlock.Transit shed: an estimated 12 tons of Class A spares, per ledgers 21 days old; hand-loading runs 4 minutes per ton per 4-person team

phases.protocol: Storm-cell procedure — when dry-storm static closes the net beyond 2 km, demolition state passes by flare: GREEN over a magazine, charges set and armed. RED over the dispatch block, firing room NOT secured, the officer's clock is live. Double WHITE, all teams to the rally point, the yard is being conceded. Flares read at 2 km inside a storm cell; nothing else you carry does.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — CLOSING THE LEDGER
phases.lead: The enemy aerospace flight takes off at T+30:00 and is overhead 8 minutes later. Your DropShip must be lifting by T+38:00 whether the cargo is aboard or not, because after that the fighters make a safe lift impossible. Plan the withdrawal like a shipping job: how much weight you are moving, which route can carry it, and a departure time that will not move for anyone.

routes.name: Route VIADUCT
routes.desc: The service road along the spine — flat, firm, 18 km at full march speed in under an hour.
routes.tradeoff: It is the enemy's reaction artery: every minute on it is spent in line dispatch's sight, and the relief column's highway parallels it the full 26 km from the district capital.

routes.name: Route SLATE
routes.desc: Gully-bottom withdrawal south toward the badlands LZ, masked to 'Mech height the entire distance — invisible to the Yard Dog, the line, and the highway alike.
routes.tradeoff: One-third movement: 2.6 hours to cover what the service road covers in 50 minutes. Usable only if the alarm never sounded or the lift window has already been surrendered.

routes.name: Route CONSIST
routes.desc: If the line holds power and the yard's flatbed consist survived: 12 tons of spares and the assault element ride out at line speed — the fastest extraction in the file.
routes.tradeoff: Dispatch can de-energize the line from the district capital at any moment; a dead consist on a 14-meter viaduct converts the extraction into a rescue.

dataBlock.Hard lift: T+38:00 — all elements aboard, or the ship departs for the alternate pickup 200 km south
dataBlock.Alternate pickup: 200 km south through gully terrain — an estimated 60 hours of movement for a lance that misses its lift
dataBlock.Aerospace clock: flight wheels-up T+30:00 from alert, on-station over the yard 8 minutes later

sidebarKernel.kernel: The hard lift is T+38:00. Decide in advance which objectives you will abandon if the clock runs out before all the spares are loaded — for example, leave the last tons of spares rather than miss the lift. Making that call now, calmly, is far better than making it under fire at the yard with the fighters inbound.

resourceGates.lackingText: Combat-drop release over a defended yard is owner-operator work; no charter accepts the liability. Unavailable without an owned drop-rated DropShip.

title: OPERATION STONE HARVEST
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. This job is deniable, and you should understand exactly how before you take the advance: the people paying you will publicly deny any connection to it if it goes wrong. {EMPLOYER} needs zone-refined germanium of the grade used in JumpShip cores, and {TARGET_FACTION} has 600 kilograms of it, in finished crystal boules, sitting in the assay vault of a deep mine on {WORLD}, waiting for its regular guarded shipment out to rear-area contractors. {NPC:intel-source}, a systems supervisor in the mine's operations office, reports the vault contents and the shipment date with 11 days to spare. That report is only 6 days old and rated reliable. Two separate factions on the employer's side are behind this — one that wants the germanium and one that wants the {TARGET_FACTION} mine embarrassed — and both will deny involvement publicly. Neither will pay you openly, so the payment is held in escrow by a neutral third party in another system; you collect from there once the job is done. The terrain problem is that the objective is straight down. The vault is on the 240-meter level of Shaft 9. There are only two ways down: the cage hoist under the Shaft 9 headframe, which takes 4 minutes per trip and carries 8 people or 1 ton at a time, or the vehicle ramp, 7 kilometers of switchbacks at a 12 percent grade rated for 40-ton mine haulers but not for anything you brought. BattleMechs cannot go below ground at all. Whatever you send down comes back up by the hoist, by the ramp, or not at all. If the hoist loses power while your team is below, the only way out is the emergency ladders — a 4-hour climb, each carrier hauling 75 kilograms of germanium and rotating it shoulder to shoulder. On the surface are the headframe, the power station, the concentrator drive hall, and a vehicle park. Site security is 1 corporate infantry platoon (Veteran, professional, well-paid) and 2 mining IndustrialMechs fitted with cutting lasers that the duty roster lists as ordinary plant equipment. The mine's rescue brigade — 40 trained personnel — also serves as militia and knows the underground workings far better than your team ever will. The nearest {TARGET_FACTION} militia post is 54 kilometers down-valley at the valley town: 1 'Mech lance, 1 motorized infantry company, 2 VTOLs. {NPC:opfor-commander} there receives a constant seismic-sensor feed from the mine, so any underground demolition shows up on the regional network even if the surface looks calm. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, plus a 6-person vault team willing to work underground.

objectives.primary: Seize 600 kg of zone-refined germanium boules from the Shaft 9 assay vault and return them to the surface and the extraction transport.
objectives.secondary: Destroy the concentrator drive hall — 6 months of {TARGET_FACTION} output lost without touching the shafts the miners need to live.
objectives.bonus: Exfiltrate {NPC:inside-agent}, the systems supervisor, whose position is spent the moment the vault opens without paperwork.

complications.name: Hoist Interlock
complications.text: The cage hoist draws from the site power station. Destroy or trip the station while the vault team is below and the cage hangs dead wherever it is; the manway climb from the 240-meter level is 4 hours with cargo.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If site power fails before the vault team surfaces: team exfil time +240 minutes, the secondary objective's demolition timing is constrained, and the hard deadline almost certainly passes with the team underground — see fork OPERATION DEEP RECEIPT.

complications.name: Rescue Brigade
complications.text: The 40-person mine rescue brigade is well drilled, equipped with breathing apparatus, and armed from a militia weapons locker. Underground, in tunnels they have worked for years, they have a large advantage: they know every passage, junction, and dead end, and they can move and fight in the dark without lights.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All underground engagements: brigade elements count one quality grade higher and ignore darkness penalties. Surface engagements: they revert to Green militia values.

complications.name: Plant Equipment
complications.text: The 2 mining IndustrialMechs carry vehicle-grade cutting lasers and work the drive hall in shifts. Inside the cramped hall their lasers only reach a short distance, but the tight space and the cover of heavy machinery work in their favor, so a fight there is on their terms, not yours.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Treat as combat units (light-vehicle band, lasers effective to 90 m) only inside or adjacent to the drive hall; in the open they are slow targets and their operators know it.

complications.name: Seismic Telltale
complications.text: Underground demolition or weapons fire above small-arms registers on the regional seismic net and flags the valley town's militia post automatically, regardless of surface noise discipline.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any underground explosion starts the reaction timeline at that moment if it has not already started. Vault entry by drill-and-cut (45 minutes, silent) avoids this; vault entry by charge (4 minutes) does not.

decisionPoints.name: Ingress — How the Valley Sees You Arrive
decisionPoints.context: The valley has one road, one mine, and a militia post 54 kilometers away that controls the only fast-moving force in the area. How you arrive decides when the enemy reaction clock starts — at the gate when you show up, or later, at the vault, once they finally notice you.

options.title: Option A — Clearcut Landing, Canopy Approach
advantages: Ground 30 km out in a logged block, approach under old-growth canopy that defeats VTOL observation
Full force arrives together; the vault team descends with 'Mech overwatch already standing on the headframe apron
disadvantages: 5 hours of approach movement; {NPC:inside-agent}'s duty shift — and vault access codes — expire at 0600
A logging skid crew works the block's east edge; on a 1-in-3 they are present and reporting within 4 hours
options.consequence: This puts your strongest force at the objective but leaves almost no slack in the timetable. The vault codes expire at 0600, so if the approach runs even 90 minutes late, the codes are dead and you must drill and cut the vault open (45 minutes, but it sets off the seismic alarm) instead of simply unlocking it.

costs.resource: 5 of the schedule's spare hours — {NPC:inside-agent}'s vault codes expire at 0600, and the approach uses up nearly all the margin before then
costs.risk: 1-in-3 chance the logging crew is working the block's east edge and reports you to the authorities within 4 hours

options.title: Option B — Ore Convoy Cover
advantages: The vault team rides {NPC:fixer}'s contracted ore haulers up the decline ramp at the 0400 empty-return run — inside the wire without a shot
Surface stays quiet; the seizure can be 40 minutes old before anyone reads a manifest twice
disadvantages: 'Mech support waits at the landing point 19 km out — 35 minutes away at best speed when things go loud
The haulers are weighed at the gate; 600 kg of boules outbound requires the weighbridge operator bought, fooled, or absent
options.consequence: This is the quietest way in but the most fragile once you are discovered. From the moment you are spotted, the vault team is on its own against the rescue brigade, with 'Mech support 35 minutes away and the ramp as the only way out.

costs.resource: the weighbridge: the haulers are weighed at the gate, so 600 kg of boules going out means the weighbridge operator must be bribed, deceived, or off duty
costs.risk: The vault team is alone inside the perimeter with 'Mech support 35 minutes away if the alarm goes up

options.title: Option C — Dawn Assault on the Headframe
advantages: Land 4 km out at first light and take the headframe, power station, and gate in one 15-minute action — every variable becomes a known
The cage runs on your schedule; the weighbridge stops mattering
disadvantages: The reaction timeline starts at first contact; militia VTOLs are overhead at T+25:00
Corporate security falls back down the ramp and holds the 80-meter level switchback — the vault team fights downhill into prepared positions
options.consequence: You control the surface for roughly an hour. Below the 80-meter level you have to fight your way down through prepared defenses, and you are doing it against a clock: the valley militia is on its way and the longer the fight runs, the closer they get.

costs.resource: roughly one hour of surface control — taking anything below the 80-meter level costs assault time while the valley militia closes in
costs.risk: Militia VTOLs overhead at T+25:00, and corporate security falls back to hold the ramp switchback from prepared positions

entries.event: Mine alarm — gate contact, seismic flag, or duty-office silence triggers the valley militia-post notification.
Militia VTOL pair launches; recon overhead the mine at T+25:00.
Motorized infantry company departs the valley town up the valley road.
Militia 'Mech lance departs; valley road transit 50 minutes at march speed.
Lance arrives; combined cordon of the mine gate and ramp mouth achievable.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+85:00 — when the lance seals the ramp mouth and the gate, the valley closes. Any element still underground at T+85:00 is besieged, not extracting. Surface elements must be moving by T+70:00.

opforSketch.composition: Site: 1 Veteran corporate infantry platoon, 2 IndustrialMechs (drive hall only), 40-person rescue brigade (Green surface / effective-Veteran underground). Relief band: 1 militia 'Mech lance (Regular, medium bias), 1 motorized company, 2 VTOLs. No aerospace inside 2 jumps' response time.
opforSketch.behavior: Corporate security defends the payroll, not the province — they fall back early and preserve personnel, then guide the militia in. The militia lance commander fights to seal exits rather than to engage; expect the cordon, not the charge.

forks.name: OPERATION GLASS KEEL
forks.trigger: All 600 kg delivered; {EMPLOYER}'s JumpShip refit proceeds at the neutral-system yards.
forks.consequence: The unit is offered the refit-escort retainer — 8 months of quiet, paid transit security with the gratitude of people who officially never met you.

forks.name: OPERATION DEEP RECEIPT
forks.trigger: The vault team is cut off underground when the cordon closes.
forks.consequence: {TARGET_FACTION} searches the mine workings intensively to find them. You are offered a recovery operation, which must happen within 60 hours — before the captured team is transferred to {TARGET_FACTION} intelligence custody off-world — at hazard rates, and again the employer will publicly deny any connection to it.

forks.name: OPERATION RETURNED POST
forks.trigger: Unit identity established by witnesses, wreckage, or the weighbridge ledger.
forks.consequence: A {TARGET_FACTION} counter-raid hits the unit's staging facility within 70 days; the delegation that never hired you declines, in writing, to fund its defense.

storyElementSeed: The cage comes up slower than it went down. The winch operator counts the cable marks aloud, flat-voiced, and the apron crew stops pretending not to listen.

is-liao.situation: Frame the deniability as deliberate Confederation policy, not nervousness. Your contact will confirm nothing except the single phrase 'stone harvest proceeds.' Your cover story, if you are captured, is that you were salvaging abandoned equipment. The Confederation already holds documents that claim the mine was Capellan property all along, ready to support that story.

declineRampKm.unit: km of switchback ramp at 12% grade

phases.name: INGRESS — THE VALLEY'S ONE ROAD
phases.lead: The valley has one road in and one mine at the end of it. The ingress options decide when the enemy reaction clock starts: at the gate when you arrive, or later, at the vault door, once they realize something is wrong.

dataBlock.Valley geometry: 54 km of valley road to the valley town; militia VTOL pair overhead the mine at T+25:00 from any alarm
dataBlock.Vault codes: {NPC:inside-agent}'s access codes are valid on shift only and expire at 0600 — after that the vault is a 45-minute drill-and-cut (silent) or a 4-minute charge (seismic flag, immediate)
dataBlock.Overnight posture: corporate platoon (Veteran) holds 6-man posts at the gate and headframe; the 40-person rescue brigade sleeps in the camp dormitory, 8 minutes from a muster bell

sidebarKernel.kernel: The inside source's report is 6 days old and good, but his vault access ends at 0600 sharp when his shift does. Stress that the timing is unforgiving: a raid that arrives even 90 minutes late has lost the codes entirely and is now facing a vault it must drill open, which changes the whole plan.

phases.name: BELOW COLLAR — THE VAULT
phases.lead: Below ground the job comes down to numbers and logistics: 240 meters down, 600 kilograms to bring back up, and every kilogram has to come out by cage, by ramp, or carried on someone's shoulders. Whoever controls the power station controls the hoist, because the hoist runs on site power. And no matter who holds what, the seismic sensors are recording every underground explosion and reporting it to the militia post.

dataBlock.Cage hoist: 4 minutes per cycle, 8 persons or 1 ton per cage — the 6-person vault team rides down in 1 cycle; boules and team come back up in 2
dataBlock.Vault entry: code entry before 0600: 90 seconds. Drill-and-cut: 45 minutes, silent. Charge: 4 minutes, and the regional seismic net flags the valley militia post the moment it fires
dataBlock.Manway contingency: hoist power lost with the team below: 4 hours of ladder climb, 75 kg of germanium per carrier, shoulders rotated every 3 flights
dataBlock.Underground opposition: the rescue brigade fights one quality grade up and ignores darkness below collar — 40 people who have walked these levels for years

phases.protocol: Hoist bell code (the mine's own, posted in the winch house — use it; a wrong sequence is an alarm in itself): 1 bell, stop. 2, lower. 3, raise, persons riding. 4, raise, cargo only. 9, emergency, surface everything. Vault team duress signal to the surface element: 4 bells then 1, repeated — cargo coming up under duress; clear the apron and cover the cage doors.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Explain what happens if the power station is damaged in a fight while the cage is in motion. The cage brakes are gravity-safe, so it will not fall — but it will stop and hang wherever it is. A cage stuck partway up, say at the 80-meter level, loaded with people and 600 kilograms of germanium, is the worst case, and no version of this plan wants it. Spell out the recovery: the emergency ladders, the 4-hour climb, 75 kilograms per carrier.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — SURFACING ON A TIMER
phases.lead: Surface elements should be moving down-valley by T+70:00. At T+85:00 the militia lance seals the ramp mouth and the gate, and anyone still underground after that is trapped, not extracting. Whatever else happens, do not let the weighbridge ledger leave the site recording your weights — it is evidence that can identify the unit, so destroy or take it.

dataBlock.Cordon clock: T+85:00 — lance seals ramp mouth and gate; its valley transit takes 50 minutes at march speed, so the commitment point passes at the valley town around T+35:00
dataBlock.Exfil load: 600 kg of boules = 1 cage cycle, then 1 light vehicle from the mine's own park — the lot holds an estimated 4 flatbed haulers and 2 crew buses, but that count is unconfirmed, from {NPC:inside-agent}'s parking-pass tally 6 days ago
dataBlock.Ramp option: 7 km of switchbacks at 12 percent, rated for 40-ton haulers — 22 minutes down in a borrowed hauler, brakes permitting

sidebarKernel.kernel: Lay out the ways 600 kilograms can leave the mine: 1 cage cycle, 1 light hauler down the ramp, or 8 people climbing the ladders for 4 hours. Decide the load plan before the first shot is fired, because if you wait until the militia cordon is closing, the cordon will have made the decision for you by cutting off the easy options.

assetDetails.detail: Systems supervisor in the operations office. His vault codes work only during his shift and expire at 0600. The moment the vault is opened without authorization, the enemy will know he was the leak, so his usefulness as a source ends there and he must come out or be left to be caught. Extracting him is the bonus objective and means carrying an extra person: 1 seat, no cargo bumped to make room. There is also an open question about his family in the company housing block. His handler has spoken to him only once, 6 days ago, and does not know whether he will leave without them.

Packed as 12 assay cases at 50 kg each, sealed with {TARGET_FACTION} assay tape — the neutral-system escrow's third-party assessor halves the release price for broken seals. Each case is a 2-person carry on stairs and ladders; on the manway a carrier manages 75 kg and 4 hours, and not 1 kilogram or 1 minute more.

resourceGates.lackingText: {NPC:fixer}'s haulers and the weighbridge arrangement are paid in advance, in full, in untraceable scrip. Below 35,000 C-bills on hand there is no convoy to ride.

title: OPERATION PAPER AURORA
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} border, {YEAR}. The sensor logs you are after look dull, and that is exactly why they are valuable. Dull means routine, routine means predictable, and predictability is what lets {EMPLOYER} plan next season's counter-raids on hard data instead of guesswork. {TARGET_FACTION}'s Array Site 7 sits on a high plateau on {WORLD}, 140 kilometers north of the DropPort, watching the approach routes with a phased sensor array. The array's raw recordings are stored on-site: 90 days of unfiltered traffic logs on removable drive stacks, 38 kilograms in total. The copies that get transmitted to {TARGET_FACTION} intelligence have been edited — convoy escorts deleted, gaps in patrol coverage smoothed over. The raw drives on-site are the only honest, unedited record, and {EMPLOYER}'s analysts want the physical drives in hand. The site layout is well known, from a report 12 days old. Where the drive stacks sit inside the operations bunker is less certain: that detail is 31 days old, so budget time to search once you are inside. The terrain problem is the sky. The world's far north is entering auroral storm season: geomagnetic storms come and go in cycles of 9 to 14 hours. At a storm's peak, orbital surveillance is blinded, Site 7's own array drops to half range, and your DropShip can land without being detected. But the same peak also kills your communications: nothing works beyond 2 kilometers, and navigation drifts by up to 600 meters for every hour of movement. Between peaks the sky watch is complete, and a DropShip on the plateau shows up clearly on every {TARGET_FACTION} sensor from the DropPort to the jump point. So you arrive during one storm and leave during the next, and the gap between storms is set by the weather and cannot be adjusted. The site garrison is 2 infantry squads, 1 light 'Mech (20-ton class) patrolling a plowed perimeter track, and 4 technicians on rotating watch. According to a defector's account, site procedure is a 12-minute data wipe: from the moment the perimeter alarm sounds, the duty technician starts overwriting the drive stacks, and at the 12-minute mark the honest 90-day record is gone. That figure comes from a defector who left 47 days ago, so the real wipe time could be shorter now. The approach road is snow-packed and rated for light units only; anything over 55 tons breaks through the crust and bogs down. {NPC:opfor-commander} at the DropPort has a VTOL section and 1 'Mech company, but they can only fly between storm peaks. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} — light, fast, and able to operate through the auroras.

objectives.primary: Seize the raw drive stacks (estimated 90 days of unfiltered sensor logs, 38 kg) from the Site 7 operations bunker before zeroize completes.
objectives.secondary: Photograph and strip the array's signal-processing rack — component identification tells {EMPLOYER}'s engineers what the array can and cannot see.
objectives.bonus: Emplace 1 passive tap on the site's landline trunk south of the perimeter, battery-rated 120 days.

complications.name: The Twelve-Minute Eraser
complications.text: The data wipe starts when the perimeter alarm sounds and finishes 12 minutes later. The technician running it sits at a console inside the operations bunker, behind one armored door. You have two ways to stop it. The reliable way is to get through that door and reach the console before the 12 minutes are up. The fallback is to cut power to the bunker at the last moment and hope the overwrite stops partway through, leaving some of the record intact.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Hard timer: at T+12:00 from first alarm the primary objective degrades to PARTIAL (fragmentary recovery, 20–40 days of logs). Cutting bunker power before completion freezes the overwrite where it stands — roll for how much survives.

complications.name: Storm Clock Variance
complications.text: The auroral cycles run 9 to 14 hours, forecast-only. Your lift window is the next peak after the raid; if the cycle runs long, you hold on a hostile plateau with the sky clearing.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll lift-window timing at mission start (9–14 hours from ingress peak, hidden from players until T+6:00). The hard deadline moves with it; the reaction forces' flight operations resume the moment the peak passes.

complications.name: Aurora Silence
complications.text: During storm peaks, communications beyond 2 kilometers fail for everyone. The lance cannot reach the DropShip, the site cannot reach the DropPort — but the site's landline trunk still works, and yours does not exist.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During peaks: no radio beyond 2 km, no DropShip contact, navigation drift 600 m/hour unless halted to fix position. The site's wired alarm to the DropPort functions normally unless the trunk is cut (which is itself logged as a line fault — response at line-fault priority, +40 minutes).

complications.name: Crust Rating
complications.text: The plateau's snow-packed surfaces carry light 'Mechs at full speed. Anything over 55 tons breaks through and wallows.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Units over 55 tons: half movement on all plateau terrain and a bog-down check on any run. The force recommendation is not a suggestion.

decisionPoints.name: Ingress — Which Storm You Trust
decisionPoints.context: Every approach uses an auroral storm for cover. What differs is how long you are on {WORLD} before reaching the objective, and what you are willing to spend to give yourself an edge against the 12-minute data-wipe deadline.

options.title: Option A — Peak Drop, Blind and Close
advantages: Descend at storm peak, grounded 8 km from the site with zero orbital observation
Shortest total exposure on-world — one storm in, the next storm out
disadvantages: Blind drop in auroral interference: landing scatter and navigation drift can put the lance 25 minutes from where it believes it is
No rehearsal, no eyes-on — the 12-minute problem is solved on the first attempt or not at all
options.consequence: This minimizes your time on the planet but makes the outcome highly unpredictable. The whole mission comes down to the first 15 minutes at the perimeter, with no chance to scout or rehearse first.

costs.resource: one storm peak, spent entirely on the landing — no rehearsal, no advance look at the site, and no second try at the 12-minute data-wipe problem
costs.risk: Auroral navigation drift can leave the lance up to 25 minutes' travel from where it thinks it is, while the objective has only a 12-minute timer

options.title: Option B — Early Insertion, Cave Lay-Up
advantages: Insert 60 hours early in a clear gap via {NPC:smuggler-captain}'s licensed survey charter; lay up in a plateau cave system 11 km out
Three days of eyes-on: guard rotations, the technician's smoke breaks, the exact walk-time from perimeter wire to bunker door
disadvantages: 60 hours of presence for ground teams with 'Mechs arriving only at the strike peak — if the lay-up is found, the team fights infantry actions alone
The charter is logged at the DropPort; if anyone pulls the manifest within the week, {NPC:smuggler-captain} burns
options.consequence: Three days of watching the site turns the 12-minute deadline into a rehearsed routine you can do in about 9 minutes. The cost is 60 hours exposed near a hostile site, plus reliance on a bought charter crew whose involvement could later be traced.

costs.risk: The charter's manifest stays in DropPort records for a week — if anyone pulls it, it exposes {NPC:smuggler-captain} and closes the unit's quiet route into {TARGET_FACTION} space

options.title: Option C — The Relay Compromise
advantages: Strike the relay station 22 km downslope instead: 1 squad garrison, no zeroize protocol, no armored door
Half the approach, half the opposition, same storm windows
disadvantages: The relay buffers only 30 days of filtered logs — analytically worth perhaps a third of the raw stacks
Site 7 logs the relay's silence within minutes; {TARGET_FACTION} knows exactly what was taken and hardens both sites
options.consequence: You trade a hard-to-get full prize for an easy partial one. {EMPLOYER}'s analysts get a useful but limited slice of the data, and once you hit the relay, Site 7 hardens and the chance at the full site is gone for good.

costs.resource: the option of ever taking the full site — permanently lost once Site 7 notices the relay has gone silent and both sites are reinforced
costs.risk: The take is capped at roughly one-third of the raw drive contents; under the contract's data-quality clause that may only earn the minimum kill fee, not full payment

entries.event: Perimeter alarm at Site 7 — zeroize begins; wired alarm reaches DropPort TOC (unless trunk cut).
Site security engages: 2 squads to prepared positions, light 'Mech moves to the perimeter track.
Zeroize completes — primary objective degrades if the console is not taken.
If sky is clear: VTOL section overhead from the DropPort. If storm peak: nothing flies; ground QRF dispatches instead, arrival T+3:30:00.
{TARGET_FACTION} 'Mech company elements and aerospace sweep the plateau the moment the peak passes.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Lift rides the next storm peak, which comes 9 to 14 hours after you arrive. Get all elements aboard within 40 minutes of the peak starting. Miss it and the DropShip sits grounded under a clearing sky, a 'Mech company inbound, and the next peak only loosely forecast at 9 to 14 hours out.

opforSketch.composition: Site: 2 infantry squads (Regular), 1 light 'Mech (20-ton band), 4 technicians. DropPort band: 1 {TARGET_FACTION} 'Mech company (Regular, balanced), 1 VTOL section (the combined-arms element on the board), 1 aerospace flight — all flight operations gated by the storm cycle. Generator should hold the company off-board until a clear gap exists.
opforSketch.behavior: Site force fights to delay, not to win — their job is the 12 minutes. DropPort response is doctrine-rigid: nothing launches in a peak, everything launches the minute it ends. {NPC:opfor-commander} will pursue onto the plateau but not commit 'Mechs heavier than the crust rating; expect light, fast, and persistent.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIET CALENDAR
forks.trigger: Analysts reconstruct the {TARGET_FACTION} convoy schedule from the raw logs within 30 days.
forks.consequence: The unit gets first refusal on the interception raid against the season's highest-value convoy — known route, known escort, known gap.

forks.name: OPERATION BLANK PAGE
forks.trigger: Zeroize completes; the raw record is gone.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} re-tasks against the relay station's 30-day buffer before {TARGET_FACTION} hardens it — a thinner prize on a tighter clock, at the same plateau's prices.

forks.name: OPERATION TORN MANIFEST
forks.trigger: The survey-charter manifest is pulled, or lay-up evidence identifies outside insertion.
forks.consequence: {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence sweeps the charter network. {NPC:smuggler-captain} runs or burns; either way the unit's quiet route into {TARGET_FACTION} space closes for an estimated 8 months.

storyElementSeed: Green light crawls across the snow while the drive stacks are lifted out one at a time, each one logged against a paper list with a pencil that keeps freezing.

merc.objectives.primary: Seize the raw drive stacks (38 kg) before zeroize. Note the contract's data-integrity clause: payment grades against days of log recovered — 90 days is full rate, under 40 is the kill-fee, and the employer's analyst decides which side of the line you landed on.

zeroizeMinutes.unit: minutes from alarm to complete overwrite

logDaysRecoverable.unit: days of raw sensor logs on the stacks

phases.name: INGRESS — RIDING THE PEAK IN
phases.lead: Every approach uses an auroral storm for cover on the way in. The difference between them is how much of the 12-minute data-wipe problem you have already solved before reaching the perimeter. The same storm that hides you also wrecks your navigation, so confirm your exact position before you are in a situation where you need to know it.

dataBlock.Storm peak effects: orbital watch blind; Site 7's array at half range; radio dead beyond 2 km for both sides; navigation drift 600 m per hour of movement unless halted for a fix
dataBlock.Cycle period: 9–14 hours between peaks, forecast-only — the lift window is rolled, not promised
dataBlock.Crust rating: 55 tons; heavier units break through and wallow at half movement — the force recommendation is a load limit, not advice

sidebarKernel.kernel: Spell out the risk a blind landing at storm peak puts on the DropShip: it descends with no navigation beacon to guide it, no chance to abort once the landing burn begins, and once on the ground it cannot use its radio beyond 2 kilometers, the same as everyone else in the storm. The ship is committed and out of contact from the moment it starts down.

phases.name: GROUND — THE TWELVE MINUTES
phases.lead: From the first alarm the site has one job: stall you for 12 minutes while the data wipe runs. Your job is the opposite: get through the armored door of the operations bunker and stop the wipe before it finishes. Everything else on the plateau, including the light 'Mech on the perimeter track, is a distraction — engaging it costs you minutes you do not have.

dataBlock.Zeroize: alarm + 12:00 = 90 days of raw logs gone; the 12-minute figure comes from a defector debrief 47 days old, so it may be shorter now; cutting bunker power first freezes the overwrite mid-pass
dataBlock.Site posting: 2 infantry squads (Regular) at prepared positions by T+5:00; 1 light 'Mech (20-ton band) on the plowed perimeter track; 4 technicians on rotating watch, the duty console 1 armored door deep
dataBlock.Landline trunk: the wired alarm works through any aurora; cutting it logs a line fault — response still comes, at line-fault priority, +40 minutes
dataBlock.Drive stacks: 38 kg in the operations bunker rack; the location report is 31 days old, so budget 6 minutes of in-bunker search beyond the planned rack position

phases.protocol: Aurora protocol (no radio beyond 2 km): the bunker element reports by flare. WHITE — console taken, overwrite stopped, clocks pause. RED — power cut at minute 11, recovery unknown. Double RED — objective lost, collapse to the rally point. The DropShip hears nothing either way until an element physically closes to 2 kilometers; designate the runner before the wire, not after.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The whole plan rests on the 12-minute figure, which comes from a defector's account that is 47 days old. Warn the team plainly: if {TARGET_FACTION} shortened the wipe procedure after that defector left, the real deadline could be much less than 12 minutes, and the team is gambling on the door with no way to know. They should hear that risk stated out loud before they commit.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — THE NEXT PEAK
phases.lead: Your lift out is the next storm peak, which comes 9 to 14 hours after you arrived. You will know it has started by the sky itself, not by any forecast. Get every element aboard within 40 minutes of the peak starting. Miss that window and the DropShip is stuck on the ground under a clearing sky, with a 'Mech company moving toward you the moment the storm ends.

dataBlock.Lift window: peak onset + 40:00, hard; the next peak after a miss is only loosely forecast at 9 to 14 hours away
dataBlock.Hold radius: all elements within 2 km of the ship from 60 minutes before forecast onset — beyond that radius nobody can be recalled once the aurora closes
dataBlock.Drift discipline: movement during the peak costs 600 m of position error per hour; halted fixes only, and the ship cannot light a beacon

sidebarKernel.kernel: The boarding window is only 40 minutes, and the lance may be spread out across the plateau when the peak starts. Decide in advance who waits behind for the following peak if not everyone can make it aboard in time, and make that call now, before the mission, not in the chaos of the moment.

assetDetails.ref: Raw drive stacks (38 kg, est. 90 days of logs)
assetDetails.detail: The stacks pull as sealed cartridges — count them against the bunker's own rack manifest before leaving the room, by pencil if the cold has killed everything else. Analysts grade the take by days of log recovered: 90 is the full picture, under 40 is a fragment that answers nothing about convoy tempo — and 1 cartridge dropped in the snow on the walk out is 4 to 5 days of logs nobody finds until spring.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Option A — Peak Drop, Blind and Close
resourceGates.lackingText: No charter crew descends blind through auroral interference on forecast-only timing. Without an owned DropShip and a crew under orders, the peak drop is unavailable.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Option B — Early Insertion, Cave Lay-Up
resourceGates.lackingText: {NPC:smuggler-captain}'s survey charter is cash in advance — 30,000 C-bills before the manifest is filed. No treasury, no charter, no lay-up.

title: OPERATION GLASS CENSUS
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. This is a deniable intelligence job, run on a need-to-know basis: you will be given exactly what you need, and if you are later questioned, you stick to that version. {EMPLOYER} wants a count, not a fight. The question to answer: is {TARGET_FACTION} actually massing a regiment-sized force inside and beneath the great arcology on {WORLD}, or is the apparent buildup a fake meant to be spotted and counted? {NPC:employer-contact} will accept only raw evidence — imagery, manifests, emplaced sensors. Drawing conclusions is not your job. The arcology is an 88-level tower with a population of 310,000, built up over the original DropPort over many years. Its freight ramp is the only route a 'Mech can use, and it runs from the ground up to Level F6 and no higher; everything above F6 is human-sized corridors. Everything you need to observe is on levels F2 through F5: the vehicle parks, the fuel storage, and a barracks block that {NPC:intel-source} says drew 2,200 ration allocations last month against an official garrison of only 800. That claim is 19 days old, and the source has been wrong once before — in a way that made {TARGET_FACTION} look stronger than it was. So the ration figure is the thing you are there to test, not a fact to trust. A single shot fired inside the tower would be a political incident {EMPLOYER}'s diplomats would spend a year smoothing over. This plan assumes your BattleMechs are never seen and never used: they wait at a remote landing zone purely as a backup for extraction, nothing more. Two more complications. {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence runs random document checks at points inside the tower — a practice started 60 days ago after an incident no one will describe. And the F3 food-market levels are close to rioting: two more ration cuts could set them off. A riot is both cover and obstacle at once — it pulls security away but it also seals the freight ramp. One last thing, because not knowing it has gotten teams killed: {EMPLOYER} will neither confirm nor deny that other friendly agents are operating in the tower. If you run into a second team, treat them as strangers — you do not know them, they do not know you, and both sides report it that way. Recommended footprint: a 6-person collection team, {FORCE_SIZE} in reserve, and the patience to count trucks for 5 days. Completing the count is how you win this mission, even though it is quiet work that earns no public credit.

objectives.primary: Deliver verified imagery and counts of the vehicle parks, fuel bunkerage, and billeting occupancy on Stack levels F2–F5 — sufficient to confirm or deny regiment-scale staging.
objectives.secondary: Copy the DropPort lift manifests for the trailing 90 days from the port authority annex on Level F1.
objectives.bonus: Emplace 2 passive sensor packages covering the freight spine and the south approach corridor, battery-rated 120 days.

complications.name: Randomized Checks
complications.text: {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence teams run document spot-checks at stack chokepoints on no posted schedule. Papers from {NPC:fixer} are good; they are not perfect.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each 12 hours of team presence inside the Stack, roll 1-in-6 per team element moving through a chokepoint: on a hit, a document check occurs — failed checks escalate to detention, starting the reaction timeline.

complications.name: Two Cuts From Riot
complications.text: The F3 food-market levels are volatile. A riot pulls security attention down and away — and closes the freight ramp gates, which are also your extraction route's first 300 meters.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If a riot triggers (1-in-6 per day, +1 after any visible security incident), all team movement gains concealment for 12 hours, but the freight spine is sealed for the same 12 hours and extraction Option routes through it stall.

complications.name: The Unacknowledged Cell
complications.text: A second friendly team may be working in the tower on a separate {EMPLOYER} job. If both teams contact the same source, or a corridor camera catches the same suspicious behavior twice, {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence may link the two and realize a coordinated operation is underway — making both teams far more likely to be caught.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On any failed document check, roll 1-in-3: the failure is attributed to 'the other cell' first, buying your team 24 hours — but the Stack's overall alert state rises one step permanently.

complications.name: Counterfeit Stock
complications.text: The sensor packages supplied for the bonus objective came through a procurement chain with a known substitution problem. Roughly 1 in 3 fails early.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each emplaced package: 1-in-3 chance it dies within 20 days, degrading the bonus objective's value at debrief regardless of flawless emplacement.

decisionPoints.name: Ingress — The Shape of the Lie
decisionPoints.context: Three different cover stories can get your collectors into the tower. Each gives you a different level of access, and each goes wrong in a different way if it is blown.

options.title: Option A — Produce Chain Infiltration
advantages: Team enters as logistics labor on {NPC:fixer}'s produce contract — daily, documented, invisible; direct access to F1–F3 service corridors
Deniable to the last layer: if taken, the team is smugglers, not soldiers
disadvantages: F4–F5 access requires escalating the cover with forged work orders — each escalation is a fresh roll of the dice
Extraction insurance is 40 km away at the remote LZ; in a hard compromise the team is alone for 75 minutes minimum
options.consequence: This is the slowest approach but reaches the deepest. Either you get an excellent count, or the team ends up in a {TARGET_FACTION} interrogation room — the deep access comes with a high chance of either outcome.

costs.resource: each push into the F4-F5 levels uses up one forged work order — you are supplied 3, with no way to get more
costs.risk: Failing a checkpoint document check means detention, and your 'Mech backup is 75 minutes away

options.title: Option B — Open Arrival, Port Cover
advantages: The unit lands openly at the civilian DropPort as a neutral merc command in transit — real berths, real fees, real paper trail of the innocent kind
Collection runs from the port district at telephoto range; the team sleeps behind its own armor
disadvantages: Port arrival means port inspection: a {TARGET_FACTION} liaison walks your DropShip manifest within 24 hours, and the unit's name enters the planetary record
Interior access to F2–F5 stays out of reach; billeting occupancy must be inferred, not photographed
options.consequence: This is safe and low-risk, but shallow and on the official record. It answers the vehicle-park question but leaves the key question — the 2,200 rations against 800 troops — unanswered, and {NPC:employer-contact} will note that gap.

costs.resource: the unit's name entered in the planetary record, leaving you exposed to enemy counterintelligence on future contracts
costs.risk: A {TARGET_FACTION} liaison inspects your DropShip manifest within 24 hours; the ration question stays open, and the fee is reduced for the missing answer

options.title: Option C — The Ridge Perch
advantages: Lance and team occupy a ridgeline 9 km out, with mast optics — no stack entry, no document checks, no civilians
Zero political exposure; nothing about this option can become an incident
disadvantages: Externals only: ramp traffic, rooftop pads, thermal bloom off the fuel bunkerage — the interior levels stay dark
5 days static on a ridge inside {TARGET_FACTION} patrol range; one curious VTOL ends the mission
options.consequence: No matter how good the optics are, you can only see the outside, so the intelligence is graded MED at best. {EMPLOYER}'s analysts get a rough, partial picture and {EMPLOYER} pays a reduced rate to match.

costs.resource: intelligence grade capped at MED, because you never see inside the tower — {EMPLOYER} pays the lower rate for partial results
costs.risk: 5 days sitting still inside {TARGET_FACTION} patrol range; a single curious VTOL ends the mission

entries.event: Compromise event — team member detained, or a shot fired anywhere inside the Stack.
Stack security seals the freight spine gates and the F1 port-side exits.
{TARGET_FACTION} MP company establishes the cordon ring, levels F1–F6; movement between levels requires papers at fixed points.
Garrison 'Mech company stands to at the DropPort; VTOLs begin perimeter orbits of the Stack exterior.
Planetary alert declared; outbound lift suspended 48 hours.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+25:00 — any team element inside the cordon ring when it closes goes to ground in the understack for an estimated 6–10 days, and the unit's reserve lance cannot help without creating the incident this entire brief exists to avoid.

opforSketch.composition: Stack interior: civil security (Green, 22 fixed checkpoints plus rovers) plus 2–4 {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence teams (Veteran, plainclothes). Exterior band: 1 {TARGET_FACTION} 'Mech company (Regular), 1 MP company, a VTOL section (the combined-arms element on the board). Generator note: the 'Mech-and-VTOL band exists for the extraction-gone-wrong case only; interior play is infantry-scale.
opforSketch.behavior: Civil security follows procedure and can be paper-bluffed; the counterintelligence teams follow anomalies and cannot. On alarm, {TARGET_FACTION} doctrine is seal-and-sieve: close the cordon fast, then tighten level by level. They are patient because the stack has a finite count of exits, and they hold the list.

forks.name: OPERATION COUNTING HOUSE
forks.trigger: The count confirms regiment-scale staging with billeting evidence.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} sells the finding upward; the unit is retained on a shadow contract to watch the Stack's lift tempo from off-world and flag the departure window when it comes.

forks.name: OPERATION PAPER LANTERN
forks.trigger: The team extracts without level F2–F5 evidence; the question stays open.
