forks.consequence: The tasking re-issues against {WORLD}'s secondary depot district with a staler window and a noted first failure — same employer, colder tone, thinner margins.

forks.name: OPERATION SEVERED THREAD
forks.trigger: A team member is detained and held past 72 hours — the point at which {TARGET_FACTION} interrogation doctrine produces results.
forks.consequence: The unit is offered the recovery: a hard extraction from the stack's detention level before the third interview, deniability already expended, the reserve lance now the loudest object on {WORLD}.

storyElementSeed: From a service catwalk, a collector counts fuel trucks through a ventilation grate, lips moving, clicking a bead counter inside a coat pocket once per truck.

is-davion.situation: Rewrite this for AFFS use against a Capellan arcology. Drop the heavy deniability framing and open instead with the analyst's plain question, the ration-count discrepancy as the lead, and a flat statement that MIIO wants photographs, not heroics, and will put that in writing.

cordonMinutes.unit: minutes from alarm to cordon ring closure

phases.name: INSERTION — ARRIVING LIKE EVERYONE ELSE
phases.lead: Inside the tower, the cover story you chose is the team's only identity, so rehearse it until everyone can answer questions about it without hesitating. The goal is to look like just another part of the 310,000 people who come and go, not like a team that was inserted.

dataBlock.Chokepoint picture: 22 fixed civil-security checkpoints plus rovers; {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence spot-checks on no posted schedule, instituted 60 days ago — odds run 1-in-6 per element per chokepoint transit per 12 hours
dataBlock.Cover depth: {NPC:fixer}'s documents pass civil security; the counterintelligence teams follow anomalies, not papers — the cover fails at the second question, never the first
dataBlock.Reserve geometry: 6 collectors inside; {FORCE_SIZE} at the remote LZ, 40 km and 75 minutes away — extraction insurance only, never rescue

phases.protocol: Contact discipline: the team holds no recognition signs for any other {EMPLOYER} asset — if a second cell touches your corridor, you do not know them, and both reports will say so. Internal marks only: a chalk tick on the F2 stairwell rail, refreshed daily before 0900. Present, the team is working. Absent 2 days running, the team has gone to ground — execute the withdrawal plan without inquiry. Duress phrase on any channel: 'the freight lift is slow again' — on hearing it, all elements drop the schedule and disperse.

phases.name: COLLECTION — THE COUNT
phases.lead: Completing the count is how you win: photograph and tally the vehicle parks, fuel storage, and barracks occupancy on levels F2 through F5, to a standard precise enough that {NPC:employer-contact} can pass it on without adding interpretation. Record what is there, not what you think it means — the analysis is someone else's job.

dataBlock.F2 vehicle parks: count by bay at the dawn shift change, 5 consecutive days — tempo is the product, not the snapshot
dataBlock.F4 fuel bunkerage: thermal readings 3 times daily at fixed hours; bunkerage draw is the one number a paper regiment cannot fake
dataBlock.F5 billeting: laundry volume, ration queues, boot racks — occupancy signs that need no entry; the 2,200-allocation figure is 19 days old and is the claim under test, from a source who once before overstated {TARGET_FACTION}'s strength
dataBlock.F1 port annex: lift manifests, trailing 90 days — copy, never remove; a missing ledger is an alarm with a date on it

sidebarKernel.kernel: The inside source has been wrong before, always in the direction of overstating the garrison's strength. So treat every figure he provided as possibly inflated until two separate, independent indicators back it up — for example, laundry volume and ration-queue length both pointing to the same headcount — and have the report name which two indicators were used.

phases.name: WITHDRAWAL — LEAVING UNCOUNTED
phases.lead: The team leaves the same way it arrived: on schedule and unremarkable, with the collected intelligence split among all 6 people so that one person being searched does not lose everything. The security cordon closes 25 minutes after any alarm — by then the team is either outside it or trapped inside and caught.

routes.name: Route JADE
routes.desc: The freight ramp, from F5 down to the ground-level gates — the fastest walking exit in the tower, 18 minutes end to end.
routes.tradeoff: It seals at T+10:00 after any alarm, and an F3 riot seals it for 12 hours. Being the fastest route, it is also the first one the defenders close, so do not count on it after anything goes wrong.

routes.name: Route ASH
routes.desc: The maintenance tunnels below Level F1, exiting through the storm-drain outlets 600 m south of the tower.
routes.tradeoff: Not sealed and not watched, but the team's maps only cover the first 200 meters — 2 to 3 hours of travel through dark lower levels where the tower's own outcasts and runaways live.

dataBlock.Cordon clock: T+10:00 spine gates and F1 port exits seal; T+25:00 cordon ring complete, F1–F6; T+90:00 planetary alert, outbound lift suspended 48 hours
dataBlock.Product discipline: imagery split across all 6 carriers; manifests carried as film, never paper; emplacement records memorized and burned

sidebarKernel.kernel: If the team is cut off, hiding in the lower levels for 6 to 10 days is survivable, and calling in the reserve lance is not an option because it would cause the very incident this mission exists to avoid. Decide in advance who has the authority to order the team to go to ground, and the exact trigger for it — for example, a second missed chalk mark on the F2 stairwell rail.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Option B — Open Arrival, Port Cover
resourceGates.lackingText: The cover is the unit's own hull at a real berth. Without an owned DropShip there is no port cover to arrive under — chartered passage puts the team on someone else's manifest with none of the armor.
Below 15,000 C-bills, {NPC:fixer} takes payment as a standing favor instead — the produce contract carries the team, and the unit owes one unpriced service on {NPC:fixer}'s schedule.

title: OPERATION GRAY CAUSEWAY
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. This is a contract job, so understand the contract first. {EMPLOYER} is paying day rates plus a verification bonus for an answer they cannot get more cheaply: is {TARGET_FACTION} building an aerospace strip and radar picket on an offshore island off {WORLD}'s eastern seaboard, or is the construction traffic just a decoy meant to look like one? The lead comes from a dockside contractor who talked too much in a mainland bar. It is 26 days old and thin, and the employer knows it — which is exactly why they added the bonus clause. What is confirmed: about 200 contract laborers rotate to the island work camp by boat, graded fill is being moved, and a radar-sized concrete pad was poured 40 days ago. What is not confirmed is everything your payment depends on. The terrain dominates this mission. The tidal causeway is 13 kilometers of engineered tidal flat between the island and the mainland, and it floods over twice a day. At low tide it carries anything up to assault-'Mech weight, for a window of 5 hours 10 minutes. At high tide it lies under 2.4 meters of moving water and the island is effectively cut off. The tide table, therefore, sets your entire schedule. The local garrison is on the mainland: 1 hovertank platoon and a militia infantry company at the coast town, 20 minutes from the causeway entrance. The island work camp has a security detachment of unknown size. The employer's best guess is 1 platoon, but that is unconfirmed — it comes only from boat-manifest head counts bought from a ferry clerk. If the radar is already operating, every aircraft within 60 kilometers is tracked and logged, which means an overflight to check on the radar would itself be detected by the radar — proving its existence the hard way and undercutting your fee. {NPC:employer-contact} wants three deliverables: imagery of the pad and any installed antenna, a measured runway-grade assessment of the graded fill, and a count of the garrison and laborers. Deliver all three and the bonus doubles the contract. Deliver a guess instead and you become just another merc unit this employer has fired. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. And remember that the tide is fixed: it cannot be negotiated with or delayed, so anything you send across that causeway has to be back before the water returns on schedule.

objectives.primary: Confirm or deny the aerospace strip and radar picket: imagery of the concrete pad, any antenna or radar plant, and a runway-grade assessment of the graded fill.
objectives.secondary: Count and document the island garrison and laborer strength with shift patterns.
objectives.bonus: Recover a soil-and-fill core sample from the graded strip — {EMPLOYER}'s engineers can date the construction schedule from the compaction layers.

complications.name: The Chart Is Wrong
complications.text: The causeway deck sits 0.4 meters lower than the published chart datum — storm subsidence two winters back, never re-surveyed. The real crossing window is roughly 70 minutes shorter than the tide table promises.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Reduce the usable crossing window from 310 minutes to 240 at mission start; reveal the discrepancy to players only if they recon the causeway before committing, or the hard way at mid-crossing.

complications.name: Surge Weather
complications.text: A storm cell offshore can drive surge over the causeway outside normal tide hours, closing it entirely.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll 1-in-6 per 12 hours of mission time: on a hit, surge closes the causeway for 18 hours regardless of tide. Any element on the island when it hits is staying.

complications.name: Two Hundred Witnesses
complications.text: The work camp's laborers are civilians on contract wages with no loyalty to anyone but the pay schedule — and no reason not to report strangers. Any contact reaches the camp office within 4–8 hours.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each team interaction with laborers or camp infrastructure starts a 4–8 hour report clock (roll once, hidden). The reaction timeline begins when it matures.

complications.name: Maybe It's Already On
complications.text: If the radar picket is live — the very thing you are there to determine — the overflight option is self-defeating and even ground elements suffer from a watched sky.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Determine radar status secretly at mission generation (50/50). If live: Option C auto-detects, and all VTOL or airborne assets inside 60 km are tracked; ground options suffer no penalty but the egress DropShip pickup must shift 60 km down-coast.

decisionPoints.name: Ingress — Three Ways Onto a Drowning Road
decisionPoints.context: There are three ways onto the island: across the causeway (limited by the tide), into the work camp by boat (limited by the camp's routine), or by air (limited by the radar). Each carries a different risk if it goes wrong.

options.title: Option A — Low-Tide Light Lance
advantages: 2 light 'Mechs with sensor packs cross at the night low tide, sweep the strip, and return inside one window — armor where the answer is
Self-sufficient: no boats, no covers, no third parties on the invoice
disadvantages: The tide clock is absolute: a thrown actuator, a firefight, a 40-minute delay of any kind strands the element for 7 hours of full garrison attention
'Mech prints on a tidal flat survive one tide cycle — the garrison will know mass and direction by morning
options.consequence: This is fast but conspicuous, and it is all-or-nothing. Either the lance crosses back to the mainland with the answer inside one low-tide window, or it gets stranded on the island for 7 hours by the rising tide, with no way for anyone to reach it.

costs.resource: one tide window — only 240 usable minutes, against the 310 the chart promises
costs.risk: Any 40-minute delay strands the lance for 7 hours under the full attention of the garrison, and the 'Mech tracks on the tidal flat stay visible for one tide cycle

options.title: Option B — Trawler Infiltration
advantages: A 4-person team rides {NPC:smuggler-captain}'s trawler into the work camp's resupply run — inside the wire, eyes on the pad, hands on the fill
Best possible product: shift counts, interior imagery, the core sample taken at leisure
disadvantages: 3 days aboard and ashore among 200 potential informers; the report clock complication applies to every conversation
If the team is blown, extraction is a boat or nothing — the causeway is 9 km from the camp and the tide does not care about emergencies
options.consequence: This can get you all three deliverables and the doubled bonus, but at the cost of the longest time exposed and reliance on a hired smuggler who has no real loyalty to you.

costs.risk: If the team is discovered among the 200 potential informers, the only way off is the boat — the causeway is 9 km from the camp and locked by the tide

options.title: Option C — Wave-Top Single Pass
advantages: One conventional fighter recon pass below the radar horizon: 90 seconds over the island, full photographic take, home for breakfast
No tide, no camp, no witnesses who can do anything but look up
disadvantages: If the radar is live, the pass is detected by definition — and detection is itself the employer's answer, purchased at the price of strategic surprise
No core sample, no interior counts: two of three deliverables stay unverified and the bonus clause dies
options.consequence: This is the cheap, quick answer. If the radar is live, your fighter gets detected on the pass — which is itself the answer, but it tips off the enemy and earns only day rates. You get no core sample and no interior counts, so two of the three deliverables go unverified and the doubled bonus is lost.

costs.resource: two of the three deliverables stay unverified, so the doubled-bonus clause is lost
costs.risk: If the radar is live, the pass is detected — you get the answer, but you have given up surprise to get it

entries.event: Island alarm — camp security report, matured informer clock, or detected overflight reaches the coast-town garrison.
Garrison VTOL pair airborne over the causeway line.
Hovertank platoon reaches the mainland causeway head and holds it — the retreat door is now guarded.
Militia infantry company embarked on boats for the island; landing within 90 minutes.
Tide closes the causeway (assuming alarm at low-tide midpoint).

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+2:35:00 — the tide seals the causeway. Any element still on the island is there for 7 hours minimum against a garrison that now knows where to look, with the only exits a guarded causeway head and open water.

opforSketch.composition: Island: 1 security platoon (UNCONFIRMED strength — generator may roll 1–2 platoons), small arms plus 2 support weapons. Mainland band: 1 hovertank platoon (Regular), 1 militia infantry company (Green), 2 VTOLs. If the radar is rolled live, add 1 aerospace flight on 4-hour call from the continental field.
opforSketch.behavior: Garrison doctrine is door-keeping: hold the causeway head, patrol the tide line, let the water do the pursuit. They have rehearsed exactly this scenario — the causeway is their tripwire and they know its windows better than you do.

forks.name: OPERATION SPRING TIDE
forks.trigger: All three deliverables confirm an aerospace strip with the radar not yet live.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} buys the follow-on immediately: a strike on the strip before radar activation, with the unit's own recon as the targeting package — premium rates for a window measured in weeks.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG GLASS
forks.trigger: Deliverables come back partial or guessed; the bonus clause lapses.
forks.consequence: The employer downgrades the unit to a 30-day standoff watch contract from the offshore shoals — dull, wet, paid at watch rates, and the only road back into this employer's good graces.

forks.name: OPERATION CUT NET
forks.trigger: The trawler or its crew is identified supporting the operation.
forks.consequence: {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence rolls up the coastal smuggling network inside 3 weeks. {NPC:smuggler-captain} needs extraction or silence, and the employer's contract has a clause about which one they will pay for.

storyElementSeed: A sensor tech sits on a 'Mech's foot at the causeway head, boots off, wringing seawater out of both socks while reading the tide table again by red light.

is-davion.situation: Invert the employer: an AFFS brief tasking verification of a suspected Combine picket site, opening with the analyst's premise and closing with a dry note that the last unit to guess instead of verify is now garrisoning a weather station.

tideWindowMinutes.unit: minutes of passable causeway per low tide

camplaborers.unit: contract laborers at the island work camp

phases.name: INGRESS — READING THE TIDE TABLE
phases.lead: The ways onto the island are covered in the ingress options, but every way off depends on the tide. Before anything crosses, re-survey the causeway against the published chart, because the chart has not been corrected since the deck sank during a storm two winters ago. Confirming the real crossing window is the cheapest and most useful intelligence on this contract.

dataBlock.Charted window: 310 minutes of passable causeway per low tide, deck rated to assault-'Mech mass — treat the chart as a claim until your own survey signs for it
dataBlock.High tide: 2.4 m of moving water over the deck; 7 hours of island isolation per cycle, twice a day
dataBlock.Crossing time: 13 km of deck — 8 minutes at light-'Mech flank, 12 at cruise; budget 20 with sensor stops
dataBlock.Radar question: if the picket is live, every airborne approach inside 60 km is a logged track — the ground options do not care, but the pickup geometry does

sidebarKernel.kernel: The tide table is the one source on this contract with no agenda or bias, so trust it over every human source in the file, including the employer's. Once you have surveyed the real crossing window, post the corrected times where the whole unit can see them, because everyone's safety depends on knowing exactly when the causeway closes.

phases.name: GROUND — THREE DELIVERABLES
phases.lead: There are three deliverables, in the order the contract lists them: imagery of the pad, a measured runway-grade assessment of the fill, and a head count of garrison and laborers. Verified answers double the fee. A guess voids the bonus, and this employer is known for firing units that guess.

dataBlock.Deliverable 1 — imagery: the concrete pad (poured 40 days ago) plus any antenna or radar plant; 3 aspects minimum with a scale reference in frame
dataBlock.Deliverable 2 — grade assessment: measured gradient and compaction along the graded fill's full length, readings every 200 m
dataBlock.Deliverable 3 — head count: garrison strength, which the employer only guesses at 1 platoon from bought boat-manifest counts, plus laborer strength with shift patterns
dataBlock.Report clock: any laborer contact starts a 4–8 hour fuse to the camp office — count it from the first conversation, not the first suspicion

phases.protocol: Trawler protocol (where Section 4 Option B is in play): {NPC:smuggler-captain} shows 2 white over 1 amber masthead light on the resupply approach — boarding clear. Amber alone: search aboard, stay off the dock. No light by 30 minutes past scheduled tie-up: the run is blown, the walk-out plan applies, and the boat does not come back.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Be clear about the difference between 'confirmed' and 'reported' for each deliverable. The bonus only pays for confirmed findings — direct evidence the team gathered itself — not for second-hand reports, and the employer's auditor will check which is which carefully. Mark every item as one or the other honestly.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — THE WINDOW CLOSES
phases.lead: The tide closes on a fixed schedule, and the garrison simply uses that to trap anyone caught on the island. Be back on the mainland side before T+2:35:00 from any alarm. After that the only ways off are the causeway entrance, which the hovertanks now hold, and open water — and being stranded earns you nothing beyond the day rate.

dataBlock.Tide closure: T+2:35:00 from an alarm at low-tide midpoint — the causeway drowns regardless of who is on it
dataBlock.Causeway head: the hovertank platoon holds it from T+20:00; the mainland exit is watched a full 2 hours and 15 minutes before the water takes over
dataBlock.Radar-live contingency: live picket = DropShip pickup shifts 60 km down-coast; add 75 minutes of coastal movement to every exfil plan

sidebarKernel.kernel: Spell out what being stranded for 7 hours costs: the contract pays nothing extra for it, and the unit risks losing 'Mechs to a garrison that now has 7 hours to act. The verification bonus rewards getting the answer, not surviving danger — there is no hazard pay in this contract, so being trapped is pure loss.

resourceGates.lackingText: No fighter-capable deck in the force: the pass flies as a contracted third-party recon sortie at 12,000 C-bills — and the contractor keeps a copy of the take.
{NPC:smuggler-captain}'s loyalty is rented by the week, cash first. Below 8,000 C-bills the trawler does not sail.

title: OPERATION QUIET THAW
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} border, {YEAR}. {NPC:defector-scientist} is a senior propulsion metallurgist at {TARGET_FACTION}'s cold-weather proving station on {WORLD}, and has decided to defect — for reasons {EMPLOYER}'s handlers judge to be about 70 percent personal grievance and 30 percent conscience. The deal: 11 kilograms of alloy test films documenting 4 years of {TARGET_FACTION} drive-nozzle research, plus the expert who can interpret them. The films are in two parts. Part one the defector carries out personally. Part two is buried in a marked cache 3 kilometers north of the station's perimeter wire, hidden during a sample-collection walk 5 months ago. The marker is one survey stake among 200 identical ones, and only the defector's memory can pick it out — and that memory is 150 days old, so finding it fast depends entirely on him. The station has a winter crew of 19, resupplied weekly by tilt-rotor from the coastal field. The crew does a personnel check every 90 minutes; a missed check triggers the station alarm, which reaches the DropPort district garrison — 210 kilometers to the southwest — at the next scheduled transmission time. The main obstacle between any plan and the objective is the icefall: 14 to 19 kilometers of crevasse field separating the station from the only blue-ice plateau a DropShip can land on. Two surveyed lanes cross it — LANE EAST at 16 kilometers and LANE WEST at 19 kilometers — both certified safe for units up to 55 tons. Off the lanes, snow bridges rated to hold nothing will carry a 'Mech right up until they collapse without warning. Pressure quakes rearrange the crevasse field without notice; after each quake, a lane is no longer certified safe until it has been re-walked at one-third speed behind ground-penetrating radar. The defector adds one human complication: a junior colleague he insists on bringing, whose security clearance {EMPLOYER} cannot verify at all — the only word for it is the defector's own. The handlers' written order is firm: the colleague boards nothing until the films are already aboard the extraction craft. Weather is the other major factor here: whiteouts last 40 to 90 minutes and cut visibility to 90 meters, and the {TARGET_FACTION} aerospace patrols are grounded by the same weather that grounds you. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, each unit under 55 tons, with cold-rated seals checked twice.

objectives.primary: Extract {NPC:defector-scientist} with the part-one alloy films to the DropShip alive and debriefable.
objectives.secondary: Recover the part-two film cache from the buried marker north of the station wire.
objectives.bonus: Photograph the station's test-stand instrumentation hall — the fixture designs are themselves restricted technology.

complications.name: Pressure Quake
complications.text: The icefall shifts on no predictable schedule. A pressure quake during the mission cancels the safe-certification of whatever lane you cleared on the way in, so the route that held on the approach may no longer be safe on the way out and must be re-checked.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll 1-in-6 each 2 hours: on a hit, a pressure quake strikes — both lanes revert to unproved status (one-third speed behind survey gear), and any unit mid-lane makes an immediate piloting check against a collapse hex.

complications.name: The Colleague
complications.text: The junior colleague's clearance cannot be verified. If the vouch is good, you extract two assets. If it is not, the station alarm sounds at the moment of maximum commitment.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Determine secretly at generation (2-in-3 genuine, 1-in-3 informer for {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence). If an informer: the reaction timeline begins 30 minutes before the team reaches the defector, with the station security element pre-positioned.

complications.name: Whiteout Cycles
complications.text: Whiteouts drop visibility to 90 meters for 40 to 90 minutes at a time, then clear without warning. Both sides are equally blinded during a whiteout.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll whiteout status each 30 minutes. During whiteout: all ranged attacks capped at 90 m, no VTOL or aerospace operations (either side), navigation drift applies off-lane.

complications.name: Cold Soak
complications.text: The ambient temperature is -55°C. Actuators stiffen and seals shrink, so a 'Mech that has been powered down or left idling cold handles sluggishly and unreliably until its systems warm back up.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any 'Mech idle or shut down longer than 30 minutes: +1 difficulty to all piloting checks for its first 10 minutes of movement while heat normalizes.

decisionPoints.name: Ingress — Across, Around, or Instead Of the Icefall
decisionPoints.context: Every route to the station either crosses the icefall yourself or hires someone else to bypass it. The buried film cache north of the perimeter wire adds a complication to all three options.

options.title: Option A — Blue-Ice Plateau and the Lanes
advantages: Full lance crosses LANE EAST behind survey gear and arrives with armor, transport capacity, and the means to dig the cache under overwatch
Self-contained — no third parties, no covers, every variable on your own roster
disadvantages: 5 hours of lane transit each way at proving speeds; two quake rolls minimum before you ever see the wire
A DropShip parked on the plateau is the loudest object in 200 kilometers the moment the sky clears
options.consequence: This is the direct approach: it puts your strongest force at the objective, but the whole operation is at the mercy of the pressure-quake rolls and the whiteout timing throughout. It is the most common way the mission succeeds, but when it fails it fails expensively.

costs.resource: 10 hours of lane transit at slow proving speeds, with at least two pressure-quake checks before you even reach the wire
costs.risk: A DropShip sitting on the plateau is the most obvious target for 200 km the moment the weather clears

options.title: Option B — Supply Flight Substitution
advantages: {NPC:fixer} staffs the weekly resupply tilt-rotor from the coastal field; a 4-person team rides the manifest in, no icefall, no footprint
The defector walks to the aircraft as cargo handling — the cleanest extraction profile in the file
disadvantages: No 'Mech support within 16 kilometers; if the colleague variable breaks wrong, the team holds a tin station against 8 security troops with what it carried
The tilt-rotor's payload math is unforgiving: defector, colleague, team, and films — the part-two cache does not fit and must be a second trip or a ground job
options.consequence: This is the hardest to detect but leaves the least room for error. The primary objective depends entirely on one aircraft and one hired crew, and the secondary objective (the buried cache) has to be handled as a separate cold-weather trek.

costs.resource: the tilt-rotor's weight limit: the defector, colleague, team, and films fill it, so the part-two cache does not fit and must be a second trip or a separate ground job
costs.risk: If the colleague turns out to be an informer, 4 people must hold a lightly-built station against 8 security troops using only what they carried in

options.title: Option C — Storm Rendezvous at the Cache
advantages: Signal the defector to walk out 3 km to the buried cache during a whiteout and meet lights there — station never sees the approach, cache and asset recovered in one stop
The team crosses only the icefall's northern fringe, 6 km of belt instead of 16
disadvantages: You are asking a 54-year-old metallurgist to navigate 3 km of crevassed ground at 90-meter visibility, with a colleague of unverified loyalty as his only companion
If he is late, lost, or down a crevasse, the team's search burns the whiteout window that was the plan's entire protection
options.consequence: This looks clean on a map but is harsh in practice. Success depends on one frightened civilian making it across 3 km of crevassed ground on foot — and the station's 90-minute personnel-check clock starts the moment his empty bunk is noticed.

costs.resource: the whiteout window — entirely consumed if the team has to start searching for a lost civilian
costs.risk: A 54-year-old metallurgist crossing 3 km of crevassed ground at 90-meter visibility, with only an unverified colleague to help him

entries.event: Station muster alarm — the defector misses a 90-minute personnel check, or perimeter contact triggers directly.
Station security (8 troops, 2 tracked snowcats) begins exterior sweep; transmission queued for the DropPort garrison's next window.
{TARGET_FACTION} garrison acknowledges; lance and VTOL section spin up, launch held for weather.
First aerospace sweep over the icefall in the first clear window (weather permitting).
Estimated arrival of {TARGET_FACTION} ground lance at the station via the southern moraine road if flying weather never comes.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Lift before the first clear-weather window, roughly T+3:00:00 — but that time is a weak forecast, so it may come sooner. Miss it and the DropShip holds dark on the plateau through a 5-to-9-hour gap while a {TARGET_FACTION} sweep hunts for exactly that kind of target.

opforSketch.composition: Station: 8 security troops (Regular, cold-acclimated), 2 tracked snowcats with support weapons (the combined-arms element on the board), 11 civilian crew. Garrison band: 1 {TARGET_FACTION} lance (Regular, light/medium per crust limits), 1 VTOL section, 1 aerospace flight — all weather-gated. Generator should keep garrison forces off-board until weather windows permit.
opforSketch.behavior: Station security sweeps by the book and stays inside its snowcat range. The garrison response is methodical and weather-disciplined: they will not fly into whiteout, and they know the lanes too — expect their ground element to arrive on LANE WEST while you watch LANE EAST.

forks.name: OPERATION ANNEALED
forks.trigger: Defector and both film sets delivered; debrief identifies the {TARGET_FACTION} alloy plant the program feeds.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} offers the follow-on objective raid against the plant's quality-control archive — smaller target, deeper in {TARGET_FACTION} space, priced accordingly.

forks.name: OPERATION COLD COMFORT
forks.trigger: The defector is lost — dead, recaptured, or never reached — but the part-two cache location survives in the mission record.
forks.consequence: A salvage tasking inside 30 days: recover the buried films before spring survey crews re-stake the sample field and bury the index forever.

forks.name: OPERATION MIRROR FROST
forks.trigger: The colleague is confirmed an informer and survives in {TARGET_FACTION} hands with knowledge of the unit's methods.
forks.consequence: {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence builds a profile: for the unit's next 2 contracts in {TARGET_FACTION} space, opposition intelligence is treated one grade higher and ambush probability doubles.

storyElementSeed: Inside the crew door, a man in three borrowed parkas keeps trying to take his glasses off to wipe the frost, and keeps being told to leave them, keep walking, count the stakes.

merc.objectives.primary: Extract {NPC:defector-scientist} with the part-one films, alive and debriefable per contract definition 4(c) — the employer's medic certifies 'debriefable' at handover, and a frostbitten asset who cannot talk for a week triggers the late-delivery schedule.

stationCrew.unit: winter-over personnel at the proving station

phases.name: INGRESS — THE ICEFALL
phases.lead: The icefall sets the schedule: 16 or 19 kilometers of crevasse field crossed slowly behind survey gear, with a pressure-quake check every 2 hours. Whichever ingress option the team uses, you either cross the icefall on foot at its slow, dangerous pace or pay a third party to fly over it.

routes.name: LANE EAST
routes.desc: 16 km, the shorter surveyed lane — 5 hours at proving speed, with one fewer pressure-quake check than the longer lane.
routes.tradeoff: Its last 3 km cross an unstable shear zone that breaks up first after any pressure quake, so this is the lane most likely to lose its safe-certification and need re-checking.

routes.name: LANE WEST
routes.desc: 19 km over older, more stable ice — it tends to survive tremors that close the shorter lane.
routes.tradeoff: 6 hours of travel and one extra pressure-quake check. It is also the lane the garrison's own ground force prefers, so on the wrong day you may meet them coming the other way.

dataBlock.Proving rule: after any pressure quake both lanes revert to unproved — one-third speed behind ground-penetrating gear until walked end to end
dataBlock.Mass limit: 55 tons per unit on both lanes; off-lane snow bridges are rated for nothing and demonstrate it without warning
dataBlock.Quake odds: 1-in-6 per 2 hours, no schedule, no precursor the survey gear can read

sidebarKernel.kernel: Explain the cold-soak problem for the crossing: at -55°C, a 'Mech stopped for more than 30 minutes restarts with stiff actuators and degraded handling for its first 10 minutes of movement — which is dangerous in the middle of a crevasse field. The practical rule is to either keep the column moving or keep the machines warmed up; letting one sit cold and stiff is not a safe option here.

phases.name: GROUND — THE STATION AND THE CACHE
phases.lead: The station does a personnel check every 90 minutes; the moment the defector's bunk is found empty, the alarm clock starts. The cache is one survey stake among 200 identical ones, 3 kilometers north of the wire, and the only practical way to find it is to have the defector there pointing it out from memory.

dataBlock.Station census: 19 winter-over crew; 8 security (Regular, cold-acclimated) with 2 tracked snowcats; missed personnel check = station alarm = transmission queued for the garrison's next window
dataBlock.The cache: 3 km north of the wire at a marked survey stake among 200, buried 150 days ago; search without the defector runs an estimated 6 hours with detection gear; with him, 20 minutes if his stake count holds
dataBlock.Whiteout cycles: 40–90 minutes at 90-meter visibility, opening without warning — both sides blind, nobody's aircraft flying

phases.protocol: Contact protocol: the go signal to {NPC:defector-scientist} is 3 clicks, sent twice, 60 seconds apart, on the station's maintenance band — carrier only, no voice. His ready sign: the lab annex window lamp filtered red for 10 minutes on the half hour. White lamp instead: the colleague is with him and the move is not clean — hold and reassess. No lamp on 2 consecutive half hours: assume the bunk check has already failed and the station alarm is live.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The colleague is the one unverified element in this plan — there is a real chance he is an informer. The handler's written order is strict and not the team leader's to overrule: the films must be aboard the extraction craft before the colleague is allowed to board anything. Follow that sequence exactly, no matter how it feels in the moment.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — RECROSSING
phases.lead: Everything that went in comes back out across the same ice, now escorting a 54-year-old metallurgist, 11 kilograms of films, and a passenger nobody has been able to clear. Lift before the first clear-weather window, roughly T+3:00:00 — but that time is a weak forecast, so it could come sooner. Miss it and the DropShip must sit grounded through a 5-to-9-hour gap while a {TARGET_FACTION} aerospace patrol hunts for exactly that kind of target.

dataBlock.Recross budget: 5 hours minimum at slow proving speeds, with 2 pressure-quake checks — plan the return at the same careful speed as the approach, even under pressure to hurry
dataBlock.Passenger rule: the defector rides on a 'Mech; he does not walk the lanes on foot, because a crevasse rescue with the primary asset dangling on the rope is the worst thing that can happen on this mission
dataBlock.Lift criteria: lift during whiteout cover when the cycle allows; lifting under a clear sky means giving up that cover for an 8-minute exposed climb-out against whatever the enemy patrol has in the air

sidebarKernel.kernel: A 54-year-old in 3 borrowed parkas at -55°C: frostbite timelines, exertion he has not attempted in 20 years, and what 'alive and debriefable' obliges the team to prevent en route.

assetDetails.detail: Propulsion metallurgist, 54. He needs corrective glasses to see and keeps trying to wipe them in the cold, where they fog and freeze — pack a taped spare pair in the team kit. He carries the part-one films on his person and will not hand them to a stranger's pack, so let him carry them to the ramp himself if it keeps him moving. His motivation is roughly 70 percent personal grievance and 30 percent conscience: the grievance makes him eager to leave, but it can also make him hesitate and second-guess at bad moments, so keep him calm and moving.

His clearance cannot be checked at all — the only word for it is the defector's spoken vouch. Written handler guidance is binding: he boards nothing until the films are aboard something. Assign 1 dedicated escort, seat him apart from the defector, and keep him away from anything with a transmit key — the 1-in-3 case is a planning fact, not an insult.

The buried half of 11 kg of alloy test films, interred 5 months ago at a marked stake the defector indexes from memory. Metal-substrate film, cold-stable — but the canister seals are not rated for a crowbar excavation at -55°C. Dig with the entrenching kit, 15 minutes, and count seals before moving: 9 canisters, or the cache is short and the debrief must say so.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Option A — Blue-Ice Plateau and the Lanes
resourceGates.lackingText: Contracted lift refuses a dark hold on the plateau between storm windows. Repriced at 40,000 C-bills charter plus 15,000 standby, pickup shifted to the coastal field — the icefall is crossed twice with the defector in tow.
The tilt-rotor crew is bought in advance, in hard currency, no escrow. Below 20,000 C-bills there is no manifest to ride.

title: OPERATION BORROWED ROPE
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} border, {YEAR}. The target of this operation is {NPC:pow-pilot}, an {EMPLOYER} MechWarrior captured 7 months ago and held at Work Camp 11 on {WORLD}. The pilot's family name carries influence in {EMPLOYER}'s court that the quartermaster corps wants to keep on its side, which is part of why this rescue is funded. Beyond that, the pilot was carrying staff documents in the cockpit when shot down, and 7 months of {TARGET_FACTION} interrogation have not yet gotten them — but a scheduled transfer to a {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence facility in the rear district probably will. The transfer order is only 5 days old and rated reliable, and it gives you 12 days to act before the window closes. Work Camp 11 sits on a plateau above the Narrows, a fjord cut into {WORLD}'s northern coast. The camp holds 240 prisoners and 30 guards, with 1 Scorpion light tank, perimeter wire, and guard dogs. The problem is the approach. From the only beach a DropShip can use, there are exactly two routes to the camp: the Narrows Road — 11 kilometers of single-lane shelf road cut into the fjord wall, fitted with avalanche gates that can seal it from either end — or the ore tramway, a 6-bucket aerial cableway that climbs 800 meters from the fjord-side mill to the camp's mill-head, carrying 4 people per bucket and taking 11 minutes per trip. The camp works a tungsten mine, and on any alarm the guards' standard procedure is to move the 12 highest-value prisoners — including your target — down into the mine itself, which turns the rescue into a siege. That procedure comes from a released prisoner's account 40 days old, so it may have changed. The main garrison is 90 kilometers south: 1 {TARGET_FACTION} 'Mech company, VTOL lift for one platoon, and an aerospace pair on alert. Between you and them, katabatic winds blow down the fjord in 2-to-6-hour cycles, grounding all rotorcraft and making the beach a difficult landing. The quartermaster's note attached to this brief points out, correctly, that the unit's transport only seats 12 — and that 240 prisoners minus 12 seats is a number with political consequences whichever way it falls. Expect your arrival to trigger a prisoner riot, and plan for it. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. The Narrows road favors no one: it traps whoever is on it when the avalanche gates drop.

objectives.primary: Extract {NPC:pow-pilot} from Work Camp 11 to the beach LZ and lift before the garrison closes the fjord.
objectives.secondary: Recover or destroy the camp commandant's interview records — 7 months of {TARGET_FACTION} interrogation product on 240 prisoners.
objectives.bonus: Extract up to 11 additional prisoners (transport ceiling), prioritized by the employer's list, which is sealed until the camp is breached.

complications.name: Dispersal Protocol
complications.text: On any alarm, the guards move the 12 high-value prisoners into the mine tunnel. Once underground, the target is behind a defensible chokepoint held by guards whose orders about keeping prisoners alive may not hold for long once a relief force is closing in.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the alarm sounds before Block C is seized, the subject moves underground: add 40 minutes of adit assault, and each 10 minutes underground rolls 1-in-6 for the guard force escalating from holding to harming.

complications.name: Avalanche Gates
complications.text: The shelf road's avalanche gates — steel and rubble barriers — can be dropped by the defenders from the camp end or jammed by stray fire. Closed, they stop vehicles absolutely and reduce 'Mechs to climbing.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Defenders drop the gates at T+10:00 if the road is contested. Closed gates: vehicles cannot pass; 'Mechs cross at 1 hex/turn with piloting checks. The tramway becomes the only vehicle-free descent.

complications.name: Two Hundred Forty Riders
complications.text: Every prisoner in the camp will try to board whatever leaves. A riot at the wire helps the breach and wrecks the load plan; the sealed priority list helps the load plan and starts the riot.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From breach +10 minutes, prisoner crowds contest all vehicle and tram loading: each loading cycle takes double time unless 1 element is dedicated to crowd control for the mission's remainder.

complications.name: Katabatic Cycles
complications.text: Fjord winds ground rotorcraft and make the beach a hazard on 2-to-6-hour cycles. The same wind that delays the garrison's VTOL platoon delays your DropShip's lift.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll wind status each hour: in a katabatic phase, no VTOL operations (either side) and DropShip lift/landing requires a control check. The garrison's ground column is unaffected.

decisionPoints.name: Ingress — The Road, the Drop, or the Wire
decisionPoints.context: The camp can be approached three ways: from below up the shelf road, from above by combat drop, or from the bottom by seizing the tramway's lower station and riding up. Each approach changes how much the avalanche gates affect you.

options.title: Option A — Beach Landing, Shelf-Road Ascent
advantages: Full force ascends together with vehicle transport for the prisoner lift — the only option that moves 12 bodies comfortably
The DropShip waits at the beach, engines warm, exactly where the exfil ends
disadvantages: 8.5 of the road's 11 kilometers are exposed to observation from the camp — surprise survives only in darkness and weather
The avalanche gates bracket the route; dropped behind you, they cut the force off from the beach with the fjord on one side and rock on the other
options.consequence: You get full strength and vehicle transport, but you give away the approach by being visible on the road. If the gates drop as expected at T+10:00, the second half of the mission is fought on a sealed road, and your only fallback is the tramway at 4 people every 11 minutes.

costs.resource: your only vehicle transport, committed to a single road that can be gated shut — the fallback is the slow tramway, 4 people per 11 minutes
costs.risk: If the gates drop behind the force, it is cut off from the beach, with the fjord on one side and rock on the other

options.title: Option B — Plateau Drop Behind the Camp
advantages: Drop cocoons through the high pass put the lance at the camp's back fence, bypassing road, gates, and 8 kilometers of observation
Block C can be seized before the dispersal protocol completes — the only option that reliably beats the adit clock
disadvantages: Mountain rotor turbulence over the fjord: each unit rolls drop scatter, and a bad roll is a 'Mech on a 40-degree scree slope or in the wire itself
No vehicles arrive by drop; the prisoner lift descends by tramway, 4 at a time, 11 minutes per cycle, while the lance holds the plateau
options.consequence: This is the surest way to reach the target before the guards can move him into the mine, but it turns the extraction into a tramway shuttle under fire — at least 3 trips to move 12 passengers down, while the lance fights a holding action up at the camp.

costs.resource: no vehicles arrive by drop, so the prisoner extraction runs at least 3 tramway trips while the lance holds the plateau
costs.risk: Rotor turbulence over the mountains scatters the drop — a bad landing puts a 'Mech on a 40-degree scree slope or in the perimeter wire

options.title: Option C — Mill Seizure, Tramway Ascent
advantages: Take the fjord-side mill (6 night-shift workers, 2 watchmen) in silence, ride the buckets up in 3 lifts — the approach the camp has never rehearsed against
Guards check the tram only at shift change, every 4 hours; a clean seizure buys the longest undetected approach in the file
disadvantages: An 11-minute one-way bucket ride, 4 persons at a time, 800 meters of cable with no cover and no early exit — if the alarm sounds mid-lift, the bucket arrives as a target
'Mechs stay at the bottom; the assault element fights the camp's 30 guards at infantry odds until the gates question is settled
options.consequence: This is the quiet gamble: total surprise if the tramway is not checked while you use it, but a deadly trap if the alarm sounds mid-ride, since a bucket on the cable has no cover. The hidden deadline is the guards' 4-hour tramway check, which can expose you well before any loud alarm does.

costs.resource: the 4-hour window until the next tramway shift-change check — spent buying the longest undetected approach available
costs.risk: If the alarm sounds mid-ride, a bucket 800 m up a bare cable is an easy target, with 4 lives exposed per trip

entries.event: Camp alarm — wire contact, tram anomaly, or road observation. Dispersal protocol begins; commandant transmits to the district garrison.
Guard force at fighting positions; high-value prisoners moving toward the adit; Scorpion crews up.
Avalanche gates dropped if the shelf road is contested.
Garrison VTOL platoon launches if winds permit; otherwise ground column departs — 90 km, arrival ~T+2:50:00.
Aerospace pair overhead the fjord in the first flyable window.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Subject aboard by T+1:00:00 and lift in a wind lull before the aerospace pair arrives at T+1:20:00 — a DropShip caught grounded under the fjord walls fights with no sky and no sea room.

opforSketch.composition: Camp: 30 guards (Regular, garrison-grade), 1 Scorpion light tank (the combined-arms element on the board), dogs, fixed positions. Garrison band: 1 {TARGET_FACTION} 'Mech company (Regular, medium bias), VTOL lift for 1 platoon, 1 aerospace pair (Veteran) on strip alert. Generator should commit the company piecemeal — VTOL platoon first, road column second.
opforSketch.behavior: Camp guards fight from the wire and the adit mouth and do not pursue — their doctrine is hold and disperse, and their orders regarding prisoners get darker as relief gets closer. The aerospace pair is the garrison's real arm: it attacks the DropShip first, every time.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN LEDGER
forks.trigger: Subject and interview records both recovered; the records show what {TARGET_FACTION} already extracted — including a leak traced to {EMPLOYER}'s march HQ.
forks.consequence: The unit holds proof that implicates someone with a staff and a title. {EMPLOYER} asks the unit to carry it quietly; two other parties shortly ask the unit not to. Political heat at retainer rates.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG WINTER
forks.trigger: The subject remains in {TARGET_FACTION} hands and the transfer to the rear district proceeds on schedule.
forks.consequence: One option remains: intercept the transfer DropShip at its ground layover 2 jumps coreward — a target of opportunity with a 6-hour window, {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence escort, and odds the contract labels 'declinable without prejudice.'

forks.name: OPERATION PAID WITNESS
forks.trigger: The raid is attributed to the unit while prisoners remain in the camp.
forks.consequence: {TARGET_FACTION} reprisal falls on Work Camp 11's population within days, and the rear-court press makes the unit the story. The employer's goodwill survives; the unit's name on {TARGET_FACTION} reprisal lists does not expire.

storyElementSeed: In the tram bucket, four people stand chest to chest in the dark, watching the cable wheel pass overhead every three seconds, each flake of rust falling like a counted coin.

merc.situation: Strip the rear-court framing to a single clause: the subject's family pays a recovery bonus above contract, in funds the employer does not control — and the employer's liaison has asked, twice, that the unit not discuss the bonus with the subject before handover.

tramCycleMinutes.unit: minutes per tramway descent or ascent

phases.name: INGRESS — THE NARROWS
phases.lead: Two routes connect the beach to the camp, and the camp controls both: it can drop the road's avalanche gates, and it checks the tramway on a schedule. The ingress options decide where your force is positioned when the gates drop. Treat the gates as a certainty, not a maybe: if the road is contested, they drop at T+10:00.

routes.name: NARROWS ROAD
routes.desc: 11 km of single-lane shelf road cut into the fjord wall — the only route that can move vehicles, and therefore the only one that can move 12 passengers in a single trip.
routes.tradeoff: 8.5 of its 11 km are in view of the camp, and the avalanche gates sit at both ends: dropped behind a force, they trap it on a closed road with the fjord on one side and rock on the other.

routes.name: THE TRAMWAY
routes.desc: 6-bucket aerial cableway from the lower mill to the camp's mill-head — 800 m of climb in 11 minutes, 4 people per bucket; guards check it only at the 4-hour shift change.
routes.tradeoff: No cover, no way to get off early, and almost no cargo capacity — moving 12 passengers takes 3 trips and 33 minutes on an exposed cable under whatever fire the alarm has brought.

dataBlock.Avalanche gates: steel-and-rubble barriers, droppable from the camp end; closed, vehicles stop absolutely and 'Mechs climb at 1 hex per turn with piloting checks
dataBlock.Katabatic cycles: fjord winds on 2-to-6-hour cycles ground all rotorcraft, both sides, and turn the beach into a deck-landing problem — every lift is a wind product

sidebarKernel.kernel: The avalanche gates are the decisive piece of terrain. Evaluate every ingress option twice: once assuming the gates stay open, and once assuming they drop at exactly T+10:00. Only commit to a plan that still works in the second case, because if the road is contested the gates will drop.

phases.name: GROUND — THE WIRE AND THE ADIT
phases.lead: From the first alarm, the camp runs its dispersal drill: 12 high-value prisoners, including the target, are moved under guard toward the tungsten mine. Reach Block C before that drill finishes, or the rescue becomes an assault into the mine against guards whose willingness to keep prisoners alive only worsens as the relief column gets closer.

dataBlock.Camp census: 240 prisoners, 30 guards (Regular, garrison-grade), 1 Scorpion light tank, dogs on the wire
dataBlock.Dispersal clock: alarm + 6:00 — high-value prisoners moving; once inside the adit, the recovery is 40 minutes of assault work against a defensible choke
dataBlock.Interview records: commandant's office, administration block — 7 months of {TARGET_FACTION} product on 240 prisoners; estimated 2 footlockers and 1 drive safe, 6 minutes with cutting gear
dataBlock.The riot: from breach +10:00 every prisoner contests every loading cycle — loading takes double time unless 1 element holds crowd control for the mission's remainder

phases.protocol: Identification protocol: the employer's sealed list opens at breach, not before. {NPC:pow-pilot} verifies by service number plus a family-supplied counterphrase in the sealed packet — accept no shouted name and no volunteered identification; {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence has had 7 months to teach 240 people what a rescue listens for. Priorities 2 through 12 verify the same way or they do not board.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Consider what 7 months of interrogating prisoners has taught the enemy. Assume the camp has practiced its dispersal drill specifically against a rescue like this one, and that the commandant's first radio call to the garrison will name the tramway as a likely approach. This comes from a prisoner debrief 40 days old, so treat it as a fair guess, not a certainty.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — DOWN TO THE BEACH
phases.lead: The target must be aboard by T+1:00:00, and the ship must lift in a wind lull before the aerospace pair arrives at T+1:20:00. So write the load plan in advance — assign the 12 seats by name, following the sealed priority list. Leaving 228 of 240 prisoners behind is a politically loaded decision, which is exactly why the quartermaster's note flags it: someone will hold the unit to account for who was chosen.

dataBlock.Load math: transport allocation 12 seats — the subject plus 11 from the sealed list; by tramway that is 3 cycles at 11 minutes each, by road 1 vehicle lift
dataBlock.Lift gate: aerospace pair (Veteran) overhead at T+1:20:00 in the first flyable window — it attacks the DropShip first, every time; grounded under the fjord walls the ship has no sky and no sea room
dataBlock.Wind rule: DropShip operations in a katabatic phase require a control check; the same wind holds the garrison's VTOL platoon, but the ground column it cannot touch arrives near T+2:50:00

sidebarKernel.kernel: Seven months of camp labor and a tungsten adit: triage standards for passengers who must climb into a tram bucket under fire, and the working difference between 'can board' and 'can survive boarding.'

assetDetails.detail: Assume the target is in poor physical shape after 7 months of hard labor, and plan to carry him on a stretcher unless he proves otherwise. The value is in what he knows, so a head injury that leaves him alive but unable to talk is still a failed mission — protect his head. He carried staff documents in his cockpit when shot down, and 7 months of {TARGET_FACTION} interrogation have not produced them, which means he has been deliberately holding out. Expect him to distrust rescuers on reflex; open with the agreed counterphrase, not just a friendly uniform.

Opened at the moment of the breach. It holds 11 names with identifying details; the employer has not explained why these people were chosen, and the contract forbids asking. Expect at least one name to be a surprise — and expect the other 228 prisoners to grasp at once that they were not chosen, which is part of what triggers the riot.
assetDetails.priority: OPERATIONAL — it is the load plan

assetDetails.detail: 7 months of interrogation product on 240 prisoners — recover or destroy, per the secondary objective. Recovered, they are evidence about a leak at {EMPLOYER}'s march HQ before they are anything else: custody seals at pickup, 2 footlockers and 1 drive, logged personally by the senior officer present and opened by nobody below the employer's liaison.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Option B — Plateau Drop Behind the Camp
resourceGates.lackingText: No charter releases drop cocoons into fjord rotor turbulence over a prison camp. Unavailable without an owned drop-rated DropShip.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Option A — Beach Landing, Shelf-Road Ascent
resourceGates.lackingText: A contracted carrier holds at the beach under the fjord walls only at hazard standby — add 14,000 C-bills, and the ship lifts without you at first aerospace contact.

title: OPERATION TIN THUNDER
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. You are deliberately not told what the main operation is. What you are told is this: for 72 hours starting from your first contact, you must keep the garrison's attention fixed on the salt pans, and {EMPLOYER} will judge your success by what the garrison came to believe, not by how much you destroyed. Your brief has everything you need for this job; the details left out were withheld on purpose, by people whose decision to do so is not yours to question. The salt pans — locally called the Glassbed — are a 40-kilometer dry lakebed west of the garrison's fuel and solar outstation. The terrain hazard is the surface itself: a salt crust over pockets of brine. Units under 40 tons can cross it anywhere. Units of 40 to 75 tons must stick to the old caravan berms, which are mapped and provided. Units over 75 tons break through the crust, and a 'Mech bogged down on the Glassbed needs a 30-minute recovery operation out in the open — which for this mission could be a disaster or could be useful theater, depending on which side's 'Mech it is and when. Dust plumes here are visible from 25 kilometers away in daylight, so being seen is not a problem to avoid — it is the whole point. Your force is {FORCE_SIZE} plus 8 flatbed trucks carrying 'Mech mock-ups, thermal pots that burn for 6 hours each, and chains to drag for dust. The garrison is 1 {TARGET_FACTION} 'Mech battalion based 65 kilometers east, with 1 aerospace wing flying a reconnaissance pass every 6 hours. The wing is commanded by {NPC:opfor-commander}, whose file describes him as aggressive, decorated, and impatient. The patrol schedule is solid, only 8 days old. The read on the commander is far shakier — it is 2 years old, from a source who has since retired, so the whole plan gambles that he still charges toward a fight. The risk is stated plainly so no one can later say it was hidden: if the garrison believes the diversion, it sends a whole battalion onto the salt; if it does not believe it, a company of {EMPLOYER}'s assets is left alone on an open lakebed with nothing for cover but its own dust. {NPC:employer-contact} will send exactly one order during the operation, using a one-time code phrase. If that phrase is HOLD THE FLOOR, the requirement has extended from 72 hours to 96, and stretching your supplies to cover it is your problem to solve. Acknowledge no other message. If you are later asked what you knew: you were given a fire mission and a map, and both were accurate.

objectives.primary: Present a regiment-credible threat signature in the salt pans and hold the garrison battalion's operational attention there for 72 continuous hours from first contact.
objectives.secondary: Destroy the fuel bowser park and pump house at the outstation — a real wound that makes the feint read as a campaign.
objectives.bonus: Withdraw the force with under 20 percent battle damage and all 8 mock-up flatbeds recovered or burned beyond forensic value.

complications.name: Crust Failure
complications.text: The Glassbed's bearing chart is 22 years stale. Heavy units off-berm gamble per kilometer, and a recovery operation in the open is a fixed target announcing itself.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Units 40–75 tons moving off-berm: bog-down check per 4 km. Units over 75 tons: check per 2 km, and a failed check mires the unit for 30+ minutes requiring a second unit adjacent. Applies to both sides — {NPC:opfor-commander}'s heavies have the same problem and may not know it.

complications.name: Six-Hour Eyes
complications.text: The {TARGET_FACTION} aerospace rotation overflies the pans every 6 hours. The mock-ups hold up from 3,000 meters; below that, a competent observer reads tarpaulin and thermal pots inside one pass.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each rotation pass, roll observation: from high altitude the ruse holds automatically; if any event has drawn a low pass (active fires, a mired unit, AA fire), roll 1-in-3 the ruse collapses — the diversion clock ends early and the FAILURE fork arms.

complications.name: Dawn Brine Fog
complications.text: The pans exhale a 90-minute fog at dawn. Sensors degrade for everyone, and a diversion that cannot be seen is not diverting anyone.
complications.mechanicalEffect: For 90 minutes after dawn: visual range 200 m, sensor range halved, the believed-threat clock pauses — hours of fog do not count toward the 72.

complications.name: The Phrase
complications.text: The main effort's timetable can slip. If {NPC:employer-contact} transmits HOLD THE FLOOR, the commitment extends to 96 hours against supply loaded for 80.
complications.mechanicalEffect: 1-in-3 at hour 48: the extension order arrives. Ammunition and thermal-pot budgets do not scale; the final 16 hours are played at half expenditure rates or the signature visibly thins.

decisionPoints.name: Ingress — How the Curtain Rises
decisionPoints.context: The first hour of a diversion sets how believable it is. You need the garrison to conclude that this is the leading edge of an invasion, and each opening move below makes that case in a different way.

options.title: Option A — The Long Walk-In
advantages: Land beyond the western rim and walk in dragging chains, building a dust signature that grows for 6 hours like a real approach march
The slow build gives the garrison time to talk itself into the conclusion you want it to reach
disadvantages: 6 hours of approach is 1 full aerospace rotation overhead before the first shot — the ruse is inspected before it is even told
The 72-hour clock starts at first contact, not first dust; the walk-in spends supply hours buying credibility
options.consequence: This is the most convincing approach but the slowest to develop. If the first aerospace pass misreads your column as a real force, the battalion commits and believes it. If that pass sees through the deception, the operation can collapse before it has really begun.

costs.resource: 6 hours of fuel and thermal-pot supply spent building credibility before the 72-hour clock even starts
costs.risk: A full aerospace pass inspects the column before you fire a shot — if it sees through the ruse, the operation ends at the very start

options.title: Option B — Loud Overture at Verro
advantages: Hot drop at the rim and strike the outstation in the first hour — the secondary objective becomes the opening statement, and burning fuel is its own propaganda
Real damage forces real response: {NPC:opfor-commander}'s file says he reinforces toward fires, not away
disadvantages: Every reaction clock starts at minute zero; the force must sustain 72 hours of attention from a garrison already committed and angry at hour one
The drop puts the flatbeds and mock-ups on the playa unescorted for 40 minutes while the strike element is at Verro
options.consequence: The diversion opens loud and must keep up the intensity. Supply is the hard constraint: at the current expenditure rate, you run low on ammunition around hour 60, before the 72-hour requirement ends — so plan to stretch the last stretch on a tighter budget.

costs.resource: ammunition: at full expenditure you run short near hour 60, leaving the final 12 hours to be sustained on much less
costs.risk: The flatbeds and mock-ups sit unescorted on open salt for the first 40 minutes while the strike element is at Verro

options.title: Option C — The Split Bill
advantages: 2 'Mechs escort the decoy column west under chains and thermal pots; 2 'Mechs strike east at Verro — two signatures, 30 km apart, reading as a pincer vanguard
If either element is hard-pressed, the other's existence is the argument for restraint: {NPC:opfor-commander} must honor both
disadvantages: Each element is a half-company pretending to be a regiment's wing; called on either bluff, 2 'Mechs hold open salt alone
Command and control across 30 km of playa, through brine fog and dust, with one relay set
options.consequence: This looks the most like a real regiment but is also the most fragile. If the garrison commits hard against either of your two groups, those 2 'Mechs cannot hold the bluff, and the operation can turn into a rescue of that half of your own force.

costs.resource: a single relay set — all command and control across 30 km of fog and dust depends on this one radio link
costs.risk: If the garrison commits boldly against either group, that bluff collapses and leaves 2 'Mechs alone on open salt

entries.event: First {TARGET_FACTION} contact report from the outstation or playa observation posts reaches the garrison camp.
Recon lance vectors toward the pans; aerospace rotation re-tasked for a dedicated pass.
Aerospace pass overhead; first ruse-observation roll.
If believed: battalion (minus) commits to the pans, deploying along the eastern berms. If disbelieved: a single company comes to sweep, and the operation is a fighting withdrawal.
Release point — the main effort's window closes; the diversion has no further employer.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+78:00:00 — break contact and reach the western rim LZ within 6 hours of release, before the battalion disengages, re-orients, and the uncommitted aerospace wing begins hunting a company-sized force on open salt in daylight.

opforSketch.composition: 1 {TARGET_FACTION} 'Mech battalion (Regular/Veteran mix, balanced weights with a heavy company whose berm problem the generator should enforce), 1 aerospace wing on 6-hour rotation, motorized infantry in support (narrative only). A pure 'Mech-on-'Mech encounter — commit per the believed/disbelieved branch: full battalion ponderously, or one company fast and skeptical.
opforSketch.behavior: {NPC:opfor-commander} reinforces toward contact and dislikes waiting for confirmation — play him aggressive on the ground, but his staff runs the aerospace rotation by the book. Once the ruse collapses (if it does), expect overcorrection: everything at once, pride engaged.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND CURTAIN
forks.trigger: The 72 (or 96) hours hold; the main effort's landing proceeds unopposed elsewhere on {WORLD}.
forks.consequence: The unit is owed quietly and specifically: next contract negotiated with an {EMPLOYER} liaison who concedes terms before being asked, plus first call on a low-threat consolidation garrison while the unit refits.

forks.name: OPERATION SPENT MATCH
forks.trigger: The ruse collapses before hour 48 and the garrison turns on the diversion force in place.
forks.consequence: A fighting withdrawal across 40 km of open salt against a battalion that knows it was fooled — and afterward, an employer who notes, without inflection, that the main effort aborted at cost.

forks.name: OPERATION NAMED HAND
forks.trigger: Mock-up wreckage or prisoners identify the unit and its employer's hand.
forks.consequence: {TARGET_FACTION} intelligence attributes the campaign; a {TARGET_FACTION} reprisal raid hits the unit's garrison holding within 90 days, scheduled for whenever the unit is contracted elsewhere.

storyElementSeed: Two crew members refuel a thermal pot inside a canvas 'Mech torso at dusk, arguing in whispers about whether the silhouette's left arm has sagged since noon.

merc.situation: Reframe the compartmentalization as contract architecture: the employer bought 72 hours of believed threat, payable against the garrison's logged dispositions, and the rider in Annex D — 'extension at employer's discretion, supplies at contractor's risk' — is the clause your quartermaster should have struck and didn't.

holdHours.unit: hours of required diversion from first contact

phases.name: OVERTURE — FIRST CONTACT
phases.lead: The 72-hour clock starts at first contact, not when you first raise dust. Everything before contact is setup, and the setup is what makes or breaks the deception. By the end of the first day, the garrison must believe it is facing the leading edge of an invasion — the three ingress options are three different ways to sell that conclusion.

dataBlock.Signature inventory: 8 flatbed haulers with 'Mech mock-ups; thermal pots rated 6 hours apiece; chain-drags raising dust legible at 25 km in daylight
dataBlock.Audience schedule: {TARGET_FACTION} aerospace reconnaissance every 6 hours, from a rotation report 8 days old and reliable; the ruse holds from 3,000 m and dies inside 1 low pass
dataBlock.The commander: {NPC:opfor-commander}: aggressive, decorated, promoted past patience; reinforces toward fires — but that read is 2 years old and its source has retired, so it may no longer hold

sidebarKernel.kernel: The whole plan rests on the commander reacting aggressively, and that assessment is 2 years old. Warn the team: if a different commander has taken over since the source retired, the assumption that he will charge onto the salt may be completely wrong, and the deception could fail because the new commander behaves differently.

phases.name: THE FLOOR — HOLDING ATTENTION
phases.lead: Holding a battalion's attention for days is fundamentally a supply problem played out in plain view: dust by day, thermal signatures by night, and fire missions rationed carefully. The thermal pots burn 6 hours each, and at full expenditure you run low on ammunition around hour 60 — before the requirement ends. So budget the whole performance first, then execute it within that budget.

dataBlock.Burn schedule: full-night signature for the mock-up line costs 16 pots (2 per silhouette); supply is loaded for 80 hours of operations against a 72-hour requirement — 96 if the phrase comes
dataBlock.Fog pause: the 90-minute dawn brine fog stops the believed-threat clock; fog hours do not count toward the 72 — budget the pause into every expenditure plan
dataBlock.Crust discipline: units of 40-75 tons must stay on the caravan berms; over 75 tons breaks through, and a bogged-down 'Mech is a 30-minute recovery in the open — bad if it is yours, useful drama if it is the enemy's. {NPC:opfor-commander}'s heavy 'Mechs have the same crust problem and may not realize it

routes.name: BERM AXLE
routes.desc: The main east-west caravan berm, rated to bear the flatbeds — the decoy column's display route, kept visible from the eastern rim on purpose.
routes.tradeoff: Being visible to the garrison also means being inspectable: anything on AXLE during a low aerospace pass gets a close look, which risks exposing the deception.

routes.name: BERM HOOK
routes.desc: The southern loop berm, hidden in the lakebed's rim shadow for 11 of its 14 km — the quiet route for resupply and pot-tending runs.
routes.tradeoff: It adds 90 minutes per trip compared to AXLE, and a truck bogged down on HOOK is out of the garrison's view — but that also means it is out of your own force's view and harder to rescue.

phases.protocol: Signals discipline: {NPC:employer-contact} sends exactly 1 order, as a one-time code phrase, during set listening windows — 0300 and 1500 local, 4 minutes each, receive only. HOLD THE FLOOR means the requirement is now 96 hours, not 72: do not acknowledge it, do not transmit anything, adjust your supply budget, and keep going. Any other traffic on that channel, in any voice, is enemy deception — log it but never reply. Between your own units, use line-of-sight laser or couriers, because the open lakebed makes radio signals very easy for the enemy to locate. Keep the garrison guessing about your strength; never give it a clear reading.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Plan for the reduced-supply endgame: if HOLD THE FLOOR comes at hour 48, the final 16 hours must run on roughly half the expenditure. Decide in advance which fire missions to cut first, and think about how a thinning signature looks from a 3,000-meter aerospace pass, so the reduction does not give the deception away.

phases.name: CURTAIN — WITHDRAWAL
phases.lead: Once you are released, the diversion is over and there is nothing left to do but get out: break contact, cross 40 km of open salt, and reach the western rim landing zone within 6 hours, before the battalion turns to pursue and the aerospace wing starts hunting in daylight. Leave nothing behind that could identify the unit or {EMPLOYER} — recover what you can, and destroy what you cannot.

dataBlock.Release math: release at hour 72 (or 96); hard deadline T+78:00:00 at the western rim LZ — 4 hours of berm movement for 'Mechs, 5.5 for the flatbeds, and the difference is the whole margin
dataBlock.Burn drill: 1 thermal pot per mock-up doubles as its incendiary: 15 minutes to forensic ash, frames and tarpaulin numbers included

sidebarKernel.kernel: Withdrawing while the garrison still believes you are a regiment is itself a deception problem. Fade the signature so it looks like a vanguard repositioning for its next move, not like a small force packing up and running — a sudden, total disappearance tells the garrison it was fooled.

assetDetails.detail: Canvas-and-frame silhouettes over thermal pots — credible at 3,000 meters, risible at 300. They sag: the story the garrison reads at dawn depends on a crew member with a pole and 10 minutes per mock-up each watch, and the left arms go first. Each mounts its own burn pot; ignition is 15 minutes to forensic ash. The bonus objective counts all 8 recovered or burned — so will the after-action, on both sides.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Option B — Loud Overture at Verro
resourceGates.lackingText: Contracted lift prices a hot drop at the rim as combat insertion: 40,000 C-bills base plus an 18,000 opposed-landing surcharge — and the crew releases after one pass, so the flatbeds ground unescorted regardless.
Without depot access the thermal-pot and chain-drag reserve cannot be topped up before commitment; if HOLD THE FLOOR arrives, the last 24 hours play at half expenditure instead of the last 16.

title: OPERATION CINDER WALTZ
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The contract reads 'demonstration of force, 36 hours, western continent.' What it actually means is this: {EMPLOYER} has an agent inside the fusion-component plant outside {WORLD}'s capital on the eastern continent, that agent is coming out with whatever they were sent for, and for 36 hours every {TARGET_FACTION} sensor, fighter, and quick-reaction force needs to be looking the other way — at you. The employer will not say any of this out loud; the liaison's exact words were 'sustained pressure, visible, west.' Charge for that secrecy in your fee. The ground is the volcanic highlands, and the whole plan works because of ash. The highland volcano has been erupting at a low level for 5 months. The Cinder Run — an 18-kilometer corridor between two active ashfall zones — lets ground traffic move under a sky no pilot will fly into. {TARGET_FACTION} air operations are grounded whenever an ash advisory is in effect, because the ash wrecks engine intakes and canopies. Those advisory rules come from published aviation notices only 3 days old, so they are reliable. Inside the Run, visibility swings between 300 and 800 meters, the air is thick with ash, and your 'Mechs shed heat 10 percent slower while their filters clog by the hour. The machines will run poorly and your techs will be overworked, but the garrison's aerospace wing — 6 fighters at the highland airfield, 40 kilometers east — will sit grounded while you work. The rest of the garrison: 1 {TARGET_FACTION} militia 'Mech company (Regular), 1 motorized infantry battalion spread across the western continent's towns, and 1 veteran militia recon lance that {NPC:intel-source} flags as the real threat — locals, used to the ash, who will hunt you inside the Run where their own air support cannot follow. That warning is 13 days old, so treat the recon lance as a live problem, not old news. Worthwhile targets to attack: the rail junction, the highland power substations, and the airfield fuel bunkers if you want to provoke the grounded aerospace wing directly. One more thing, because employers behave like employers: the liaison's timeline has the agent's extraction window closing at hour 36, but this employer's last 2 jobs had windows that ran late. Stock supplies for 48 hours, and if the window holds at 36 the surplus is profit. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, with double intake filters and a written maintenance reserve, because the ash gets into everything you own by hour 12 and the contract's wear-and-tear clause says nothing about volcanic conditions.

objectives.primary: Sustain visible offensive pressure on the western continent for 36 continuous hours, holding the garrison's aerospace wing, militia company, and QRF attention west of the volcano's meridian.
objectives.secondary: Destroy the rail junction's switching yard — measurable damage that justifies the garrison's continued western focus after you leave.
objectives.bonus: Plant the prepared evidence kit (pirate-band transmitter logs, third-party shell casings) at one engagement site, surviving forensic review.

complications.name: Wind Shift
complications.text: The ashfall map is a weather product, not a wall. A wind shift can clear your corridor — handing the sky back to 6 fighters — or close it tighter, cutting your own mobility and the DropShip's lift lane.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll wind each 3 hours: 1-in-6 the Run clears for 6 hours ({TARGET_FACTION} air operations resume — treat as HIGH threat escalation); 1-in-6 ashfall thickens (visibility 150 m, all movement -1, lift lane WHISKEY closed).

complications.name: The Volcano Clears Its Throat
complications.text: A tremor event doubles the ash column and grounds all flight operations — including yours. The DropShip cannot lift, land, or shift position for the duration.
