complications.mechanicalEffect: 1-in-6 per 12 hours: tremor event — no flight operations either side for 6 hours; if it lands inside your extraction window, the hard deadline extends with the unit still in contact.

complications.name: The Window Slips
complications.text: The asset's exfiltration runs late, as this employer's windows do. The request for 12 more hours arrives through the liaison as if it had always been the plan.
complications.mechanicalEffect: 1-in-2 at hour 30: extension to 48 hours. No renegotiation channel exists mid-operation; refusing forfeits the completion bonus, accepting strains ammunition and filter budgets already at planned margins.

complications.name: The Locals
complications.text: The veteran recon lance hunts inside the Run on the theory — correct — that you are using their weather. They know which gullies channel the ash and which stay clear.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From hour 6, roll 1-in-6 per 6 hours of Run transit: meeting engagement at 300 m or less, the recon lance with initiative and pre-plotted withdrawal routes. They break contact at 30 percent damage and report everything.

decisionPoints.name: Ingress — What You Pay the Volcano
decisionPoints.context: There are three ways onto the western continent, each costing you something different: heavy wear on your machines, exposure to enemy air power, or a weaker, less believable demonstration. Remember the diversion only works if the garrison is convinced the threat is real.

options.title: Option A — Up the Cinder Run
advantages: Drop upwind and transit the Run's full 18 km under ash cover — untouchable from the air for the entire approach
Emerging from terrain the garrison considers impassable buys the demonstration instant credibility: whoever you are, you came prepared
disadvantages: 12+ hours of ash transit before the first objective: heat dissipation -10 percent, filters degrading, and the locals' recon lance hunting the same corridor
Every hour in the Run adds maintenance costs the contract's wear clause will not reimburse, eating into the unit's profit
options.consequence: The garrison takes the threat seriously because the approach itself was serious and well-prepared. The cost is that the unit's techs are left with about a quarter's worth of ash-abrasion repairs, and recovering those costs from the employer becomes a separate negotiation.

costs.resource: your double stock of intake filters, used up by hour 12; the written maintenance reserve is spent and not reimbursed, since the wear clause does not cover volcanic conditions
costs.risk: The local recon lance hunts the same corridor, holding the initiative and using pre-planned withdrawal routes

options.title: Option B — Coastal Cannery Landing
advantages: Ground at the abandoned cannery anchorage outside the ash zones — clean machines, clean filters, conventional approach on firm coast road
Full mobility and heat performance for the entire 36 hours; the demonstration fights at specification
disadvantages: Outside the ash umbrella, the aerospace wing flies: 6 fighters against a force whose entire job is to remain visibly, findably present
The landing is logged by the coastal watch within 2 hours — the garrison's timeline starts before the demonstration does
options.consequence: This is a straightforward fight that you win or lose on timing: keep the garrison's attention while never letting the 6 fighters catch your force concentrated. With no ash cover, there is nowhere to hide if it goes wrong.

costs.risk: Six fighters can fly against a force whose whole job is to stay visible and findable, and the coastal watch logs your landing within 2 hours

options.title: Option C — The Feint Within the Feint
advantages: The DropShip flies 3 false approach burns over 12 hours while only 2 'Mechs actually ground via drop cocoon — the sensor picture says battalion, the invoice says economy
Minimum exposure, minimum wear, and the DropShip remains free to reposition for extraction anywhere on the coast
disadvantages: 2 'Mechs must generate 36 hours of regiment-credible pressure; one lost machine halves the entire operation
If the garrison's sensor techs call the bluff — and false burns are a known trick — the diversion dies on day one with the asset still inside the plant
options.consequence: This is the cheapest way to run the contract and the most fragile. If it works, the profit is excellent; if the bluff is called, the employer's agent is left exposed because of your cost-cutting, and the failure damages the unit's reputation.

costs.resource: the DropShip's flight hours, spent flying decoy approaches instead of standing by to extract the force
costs.risk: If the enemy's sensor crews see through the bluff, the diversion fails on day one, the employer's agent is left exposed, and the unit's reputation suffers

entries.event: Garrison TOC logs first contact on the western continent; aerospace wing requests launch.
Launch denied — ash advisory in effect (this is the plan working). Recon lance ordered into the Run instead.
Ground QRF company moves on the Run's south mouth; infantry battalion elements begin concentrating from the western towns.
Second militia task force staging at the highland airfield; aerospace wing holds at readiness for any wind shift.
Contracted release — the asset's window closes (subject to the slip complication).

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Break contact by T+38:00:00 and lift through clear-air lane WHISKEY within 90 minutes of the next seismic all-clear. Miss the lane and the unit sits ash-bound on a hostile continent for a rough 3 to 6 days, unpaid past hour 48 by a contract that calls the weather force majeure.

opforSketch.composition: 1 {TARGET_FACTION} militia 'Mech company (Regular, medium/heavy bias, road-bound by preference), 1 motorized infantry battalion (Green, dispersed — narrative only), 1 veteran recon lance (lights, ash-acclimated — the generator's quality outlier), 6 aerospace fighters (Regular) gated by ash advisories. A pure 'Mech-on-'Mech encounter on the board; commit the recon lance early and often; everything else arrives in doctrine order.
opforSketch.behavior: The militia company defends infrastructure and waits for air cover that keeps not coming. The recon lance free-hunts inside the Run under standing orders and personal grudge — it is the only OPFOR element that behaves like it wants to be there. The fighters launch the instant any wind shift permits, with the DropShip as priority one.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN BILL
forks.trigger: The asset exits on schedule; attribution settles on pirates per the planted evidence.
forks.consequence: The employer pays the completion bonus plus an unitemized 'logistics adjustment' — the silence premium — and {NPC:employer-contact} becomes a recurring patron who asks for the unit by name and never explains the jobs.

forks.name: OPERATION ASH RECEIPT
forks.trigger: The diversion collapses early or the asset is taken at the plant — and recovered materials trace toward the unit's drop zone.
forks.consequence: The unit is publicly named in {TARGET_FACTION} broadcasts within 10 days. The employer offers one remedy, off the books: a return raid to recover or corrupt the forensic evidence held at the western continent's constabulary annex.

forks.name: OPERATION CROWDED SKY
forks.trigger: A wind shift clears the ash during extraction and the aerospace wing catches the DropShip on lift.
forks.consequence: A running aerospace engagement from the deck to the jump point — 6 fighters in relays against one ship's transit. The contract's force majeure clause covers the weather; nothing covers the hull.

storyElementSeed: A tech taps an intake filter against a 'Mech's shin and watches gray talc pour out like an hourglass emptying, then writes a number on the housing in grease pencil, higher than yesterday's.

is-steiner.situation: Reframe as an LCAF internal brief: the demonstration is officially deniable training attrition for the militia district, the asset is a Loki property nobody in this room has heard of, and the social note appended observes that the district's graf has aerospace warranty contracts with the firm whose fighters will not fly — which is, of course, a coincidence.

phases.name: INGRESS — UNDER THE ASH
phases.lead: The three ways onto the western continent are covered in the ingress options, and all three end with the unit visibly committed to the fight — the whole point is to be seen, so a diversion that stays hidden fails the contract. Whatever lands, the intake filters begin clogging from hour 1 and the maintenance reserve starts being used up; record that wear as you go, or you will have a hard time billing the employer for it later.

dataBlock.Ash umbrella: {TARGET_FACTION} air operations stand down under ash advisories, per published aviation notices only 3 days old and reliable; the 6 fighters at the highland airfield, 40 km east, fly the moment a wind shift clears them a corridor
dataBlock.The Cinder Run: 18 km between active ashfall zones; visibility cycling 300–800 m; heat dissipation -10 percent inside; filters crusting by the hour
dataBlock.Garrison spread: 1 militia 'Mech company (Regular), 1 motorized infantry battalion dispersed across the western towns, and 1 veteran recon lance — local, ash-acclimated, the file's real problem, per a report 13 days old

sidebarKernel.kernel: Keep a running filter log: write down one wear figure per intake per watch. By hour 12 the ash has gotten into everything, and those logged numbers are the evidence the unit will use to argue for reimbursement of the post-contract refit, since the wear clause does not cover volcanic conditions.

phases.name: THE DEMONSTRATION — 36 HOURS VISIBLE
phases.lead: For 36 hours the unit's job is to stay findable, but on its own terms: strike a target, move on, be seen leaving, and be reported turning up somewhere that looks more threatening. The garrison must keep believing the threat is growing, not shrinking. Hit the rail junction first, the substations next, and the airfield fuel bunkers only if you want to directly provoke the grounded aerospace wing.

dataBlock.Target menu: the rail junction switching yard (the secondary objective — measurable, defensible damage); the highland power substations; the airfield fuel bunkers — the option that makes 6 grounded fighters take the weather personally
dataBlock.Pressure standard: 1 visible engagement or demolition per 6-hour block, minimum — a quiet block lets the garrison staff resume thinking about the eastern continent
dataBlock.The slip: 1-in-2 at hour 30 that the window extends to 48; supplies loaded to 48 make the difference profit — short of that, the last 12 hours are rationed theater

phases.protocol: Attribution discipline: plant the prepared evidence kit (pirate-band transmitter logs, third-party shell casings) at only 1 engagement site. Planting it at 2 sites creates a repeated pattern that investigators can recognize as staged. Leave nothing bearing unit markings anywhere; burn to the frame whatever you cannot carry off. Keep the liaison channel receive-only: 'sustained pressure, visible, west' is the entire order, and the unit should quote it back word-for-word on the invoice.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The line between staying visible and getting caught is displacement discipline: move after every strike and never attack along the same axis twice. The local recon lance has pre-planned withdrawal routes, so treat those routes as a guide to where you should not follow them into an ambush.

phases.name: EXTRACTION — LANE WHISKEY
phases.lead: Break contact by T+38:00:00 and lift out through the one clear-air corridor, lane WHISKEY, within 90 minutes of the next seismic all-clear. The contract treats the weather as force majeure, so it pays nothing extra for delays — but it also does not protect the ship, and being stuck ash-bound on a hostile continent for 3 to 6 days earns nothing past hour 48 while leaving the DropShip exposed.

dataBlock.Lane WHISKEY: the one clear-air lift corridor between the ashfall zones — closed by thickening ashfall (1-in-6 per 3 hours) and by any tremor event (no flight, either side, 6 hours)
dataBlock.Break-contact budget: contracted release T+36:00:00, slip-adjusted to 48; allow 2 hours from final engagement to the lift point — the recon lance reports everything, so the last displacement is the one that has to be real
dataBlock.Miss price: a rough 3 to 6 days ash-bound, unpaid past hour 48, with 6 fighters waiting on the first wind shift

sidebarKernel.kernel: There are only 90 minutes between the seismic all-clear and the lane closing again. Walk through the timing: how long the ship needs to spool up, how much ash the drives can tolerate on the climb-out, and where the line falls between a lift the ship comes through intact and one that does lasting damage to it.
